entries.text: Star Bazaar
A small company in a shared, indifferent sky.

The crew brings a kettle into the control post. You clear a place beside the radio. The name {company} is still wet on the charter.

On the map, home is a dock with its lamps on. Past it are worlds you have yet to see. Some have goods to send. Some are waiting for what they cannot make.

The Star Bazaar is only a name on the charter. You could build a place where those crews meet. Goods will have to move. Worlds will have to grow. Someone will have to keep the ships flying while the halls go up.

You pull the chair in. A cup lands beside your hand. The crew leans over the map with you.
entries.place: Preface screen, the text when the CEO has none of their own; {company} is the player's company name

entries.text:
Marek lays a worn bolt on the desk at {company}. He kept other people's ships flying with parts like this. Whenever he asked to buy spares in bulk, someone passed the form back.

The orders are his to sign now. Your Tramp costs less to keep running. Marek checks its upkeep before he looks at the hold. The yard hands who backed him will know where to come if the work dries up.

Old contacts still call before bad news reaches the board. Their warning gives you time to act. It will not put goods in storage or feed a waiting world.

The Star Bazaar begins with loads of Minerals, carried where people need them. Marek wants to stand on its floor and know what holds it up. He wants the hands who built it to stand there too.

Read the home world's orders. Find what it has and where it is wanted. Set a route running. The bolt can stay on the desk. There is work for the ship.
entries.place: Preface screen, CEO Marek Voss; {company} is the company name

entries.text:
As a broker, Idris Kane bought lunch for people who took his buyers. He remembered what they ate. The famous smile stayed on while he read the bill.

Now {company} has a Dart and a light hold to fill. Idris sells hard and spends freely. A crew's pay is harder to smooth over than a price. They have put their work things aboard.

For Idris, the Star Bazaar means a table buyers come back to. Blooms beside the plates. His name over the hall. He has talked about it at enough lunches. People have begun asking when they can see it.

The home market's price tips are on your board as trade starts. They will not stay there long. Idris pulls his chair close. Read the prices, set your orders, and find who needs the cargo.
entries.place: Preface screen, CEO Idris Kane; {company} is the company name

entries.text:
Sela Oru checks the straps in the hold. On the rim, she learned what shifts when a ship turns hard. She came home from lanes other crews would not take. Her crews brought the powder home with her.

There is a plan beside the route board, with spare plans beneath. {company} is on the top sheet. These are your credits, your ships, and the crews who will wait for orders. An idle Bulkhead still costs upkeep. Sela taps the blank space where its first route belongs.

She can make that first lane carry more cargo. The Flagship has a few bursts of speed to spend. Once spent, they will not come back. Sela keeps her hand clear of the Boost switch.

The Star Bazaar could give the far posts a place to meet. Crews could read the same terms and ask for the next load. First, a ship must earn enough to keep flying. Sela pulls up the home world's board. Find what it needs. Put the hold to work.
entries.place: Preface screen, CEO Sela Oru; {company} is the company name

entries.text:
The clerk has written {company} on a fresh card. Tamsin Hale sets it beside her old clerk cards. She grew up in the Bazaar's docking rings. She knows who keeps spare forms, and who stays late.

She trades Biotech from a Skerrit, a hull she knows. Her contract orders ask for more cargo. Fill them and they pay more. If she cannot deliver, she must face the clerks across the same desks.

She wants to raise a Star Bazaar those clerks can work in. A place with stock behind the promises. She runs her thumb over the new card's edge. There is room on the back for more names.

Your company has a ship waiting. Read the food and energy orders. Send the Flagship to find the next dock, then set a lane. Tamsin has left her pen beside the card.
entries.place: Preface screen, CEO Tamsin Hale; {company} is the company name

entries.text: A run has one Star Bazaar. Choose the system with care, then press Found the Bazaar here in its Space Storage.
The Bazaar is built in stages. Each needs goods in its Space Storage and worlds at a tier.

entries.text: The goods are held in the Star Bazaar's own Space Storage. Buy them at a world and send them there.

entries.text: Buy the goods at a world and send them to the Star Bazaar. The Bazaar panel shows the steps.
The last stage posts the Opening: a gig to fly the charter cargo to the Star Bazaar.

entries.text: Accept it on the gig board (J), then fly the Flagship to the Star Bazaar. That opens it and wins the run.
Your first world has grown a tier. Worlds grow when your sales meet their needs.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first world reaches tier 1

entries.text: Each tier opens more and leads to a capital. Open a world card to see what it needs next.
Grown worlds pay tax at the end of each cycle. The credits are added to your cash.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first cycle in which worlds pay tax

entries.text: More tiers mean more tax. Keep worlds supplied so they keep growing.
A Restless world is losing growth progress because one of its needs is short.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first world turns Restless

entries.text: Sell it the short good, or send stock there. Meeting every need stops the loss.
A world is Hungry: last cycle it did not get enough of a good it needs, so it now pays extra for it.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first Hungry chip appears on a need row

entries.text: Find the Hungry tag in a world's Needs list. Deliver that good there first: it pays more and fills the need.
A full lane cannot take another ship. It can be upgraded instead.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first full lane shows the Upgrade route button, or an add-ship click is refused as full

entries.text: Open the world the route starts from and press Upgrade route. One fee, a better margin on every trip.
A hub keeps the worlds near it fed, using ships from its own pool.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first world can be made a hub (right after TIP_CAPITAL)

entries.text: One hub per system. Press Make hub, then add ships. It buys only what the worlds need, below the planet price.
A dead world takes a mining platform, not a trading post.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the Flagship first arrives at a dead world

entries.text: Once it stands you can mine there and route what it gives. Mining needs Prospecting.
Exploration mode flies the Flagship to each unknown world here and builds its post.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the Ships panel is opened first while an unknown world is left in the system

entries.text: Each post costs credits, so it waits at a world while cash is short. Press the button again to stop.
Dock lets the Flagship load goods from this world's storage and unload them there. The hold has limited room.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the dock sheet opens for the first time

entries.text: Unload to storage moves goods into Company storage here. Time is paused while you are docked.
Boost speeds your Flagship up for the rest of the flight. Press Boost on the ship panel.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the Flagship first boosts

entries.text: Use it on straight legs to beat a deadline. Turning stays slow, and Boosts do not refill.
The gig board (J) lists offers for the Flagship. Accept one to get a map marker.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first gig appears on the board

entries.text: Compare ETA with the deadline before you accept. You can take one gig at a time.
A tinted ship belongs to a trading house. Houses cause price drops, shortages or higher trip costs.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first house convoy appears

entries.text: Click a tinted ship to see its house's name and the kind of market change it brings.
Flood: a sell price dips. Shortage: a world needs more and pays more. Congestion: trip cost rises.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first house weather lands on a world

entries.text: Move goods to ride it out, or wait. Forecast skills give more cycles of warning.
Prospecting lets a route start at an asteroid cluster. Clusters move round the sun.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: Prospecting is learned

entries.text: Goods at a cluster are free, you pay only the lane. A cluster runs empty and never refills.
A dead world has no market. You mine it for goods no living world makes.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first dead world is open for mining

entries.text: Mining is limited each cycle. The stock never runs out. Use routes to move what you mine.
Raiders gather at a dead world you have not reclaimed. They may hit a lane in its system.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first raid warning appears

entries.text: A raid costs part of a trip. Cargo pods may drift near: fly the Flagship to pick them up.
Salvage is a one-time payout for goods that could not be kept or sold on your lanes.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first salvage payout

entries.text: It pays less than a Sell order. Add a Sell order, or make room, to keep more.
A workshop turns stock in Space Storage into new goods each cycle. Build it once.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the first workshop becomes available to build

entries.text: With an input missing it stalls and says what it needs. Send the inputs to Space Storage.
The Fabric turns mined goods into a new good at the trading post.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the Fabric becomes available to build

entries.text: It crafts only when you switch a recipe on in Space Storage. Send it the goods first.
The Fabric can build a Null Core. It is built once and fitted to one ship.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the Fabric is built

entries.text: That ship has a lower trip cost and is safe from raids. Fit it to the ship on your busiest lane.
Space Storage is one big store for each system. Goods reach it when you send them.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: Space Storage is learned

entries.text: Workshops, link upkeep, Storage Links and routes you send from it take stock out. Click its station to see stock.
A Storage Link joins the Space Storages of two systems. It moves goods only, never credits.
entries.place: Tip card line; trigger: the Storage Link becomes available

entries.text: It costs goods to build and energy each cycle. With no energy it goes dormant, and may collapse.

entries.text: Each system has its own Space Storage. A later Bazaar stage needs a world in another system.

entries.text: Dross Salt
Grey salt cut from a dead world. A raw mined good that nobody tastes twice.
Nullglass
Dark glass cut from a dead world. A raw mined good that hums faintly in the hold.
Lattice Plate
Dense plate, built rather than dug. A crafted good, heavy with the work in it.
Blast Powder
Grey grit in sacks; every fleet starts here. A trade good.
Hothouse Blooms
Petals picked at dawn; scent is the cheapest status. A trade good.
Energy
Bulk power for any world with a lamp to light. A raw good that every trade leans on.
Food
Plain staple rations. A raw good that everyone needs and nobody boasts about.
Rivets
Metal pins for ships. Bought at Voltara, sold at the system 2 yards. A trade good.
Munitions
Loaded and counted; the Plan wants them. A crafted good.
Weapons
Rail carbines and gun racks in crates. A crafted good.
Musk
A strong scent, sold by the drop. A luxury trade good.
Attar
Bottled scent, pressed from blooms. A crafted luxury good.
Vault Cask
A sealed cask from the far reach. The Star Bazaar's last stage cannot be finished without it.
Cold Gems
Cut stones with a cold inner light. A crafted luxury, valued for being looked at.
Metal Ingots
Metal bars, stacked and stamped. A crafted good.
Furnace Alloy
Hard metal blended to a strict recipe. The finest crafted good of its kind.
Jar Spores
Dry spores in sealed jars, handled with gloves. A trade good.
Medicine
Clinic stock in cold boxes. A crafted good.
Seed Stock
Seed stock that grows to order. The finest crafted good of its kind.

entries.text: A garrison has a war to feed

The Admiralty wills Ashgate's high-ring garrison to keep fighting, and Quartermaster Hanno Sulo wills the invoices to match. He bought your first cargo. {bot1} once sent him painted ballast marked as shells. He offers a standing contract with a deposit, or cash by the lot.
Sign the contract
Get: Military volume up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits as the deposit to the garrison. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather comes a little later.
The contract is signed

Sulo signed with a seal and kept {bot} as a second source, on probation. Orders now come on a schedule and the deposit cost you credits, so Military volume rises for a while. {bot}'s next weather comes a little later. Each crate is read a litany on the dock, and one rattled.
entries.place: MIL_A1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather comes a little later.
Sell by the lot
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Military volume down a little for a few cycles; {bot3}'s next weather lands a little harder. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands a little softer.
Sold by the lot

Sulo counted the cargo against the estimate and paid cash at the dock. Your own orders dip for a few cycles while the berth stands empty. {bot3}'s next weather lands a little harder. {bot}, found with its painted ballast, sees its next weather land a little softer.
entries.place: MIL_A1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands a little softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little harder.
Two fleets claim the same stock

Your contract holds. Two fleets, each sworn to a different estimate, order the same stock in one cycle, and the Admiralty wills both served first. {bot3} brokers between them and bills both. {bot1} serves one fleet. Fill orders in dock order, or by contract term.
entries.place: MIL_A2 choice screen body after opt_a of MIL_A1

entries.text: The garrison has its cargo. Two fleets, each sworn to a different estimate, order the same stock in one cycle, and the Admiralty wills both served first. {bot3} brokers between them and bills both. {bot1} serves one fleet. Fill orders in dock order, or by contract term.
entries.place: MIL_A2 choice screen body after opt_b of MIL_A1

entries.text: Fill orders by dock
Get: Military price up a little for a while. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
Orders filled by dock

Orders went out in dock order, and each fleet was told the other had waited longer. The bidding lifts Military prices a little for a while, and two sets of berths raise Ship upkeep a little. {bot}, the go-between, is one messenger too many: its next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: MIL_A2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Fill orders by term
Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Munitions Line. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the stock. Weather: {bot1} {cut}.
Orders filled by term

Orders went out by term. The fleet {bot1} does not serve held better terms. Its engineers left notes, and your engineer Tavi Brask read them to the press. Tech progress came in. {bot}'s client fell behind, so {bot}'s next weather is held back. The stock cost credits.
entries.place: MIL_A2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: {cut_std}.
Sulo sells a stolen ledger

Your orders went out in dock order. Sulo, who changed posts and not habits, waits on the dock with a case: {bot1}'s ledger of clients and berths, copied by hand at night, sealed with the Quartermaster-Saint's thumb. He names a price. A ledger is only a list until it is read.
entries.place: MIL_A3 choice screen body after opt_a of MIL_A2

entries.text: Your orders went out by contract term. Sulo, who changed posts and not habits, waits on the dock with a case: {bot1}'s ledger of clients and berths, copied by hand at night, sealed with the Quartermaster-Saint's thumb. He names a price. A ledger is only a list until it is read.
entries.place: MIL_A3 choice screen body after opt_b of MIL_A2

entries.text: Hand it to your buyers

Get: {cash_in} credits; Military volume up a little for a while. Cost: Ship upkeep up a little for a while; {bot3}'s weather lands a little harder. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The ledger goes to buyers

Your buyers read the ledger aloud and called on every client it listed. Cash came in and orders rose, and the extra hulls raise Ship upkeep a little for a while. {bot}'s next weather lands clearly softer. Sulo sold a second copy to {bot3}, whose weather lands a little harder.
entries.place: MIL_A3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little harder.
Hand it to your workshop
Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Munitions Line. Cost: {cash_out} credits to the quartermaster. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands a little softer, and {bot3}'s comes a little later.
The ledger goes to the shop

Your workshop set the ledger's parts and casting notes beside your own. Tech progress came in at the Munitions Line, and Sulo's price cost credits. {bot}'s next weather lands a little softer, and {bot3}, listed too, sends its next weather a little later. Brask thanked the book.
entries.place: MIL_A3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands a little softer.
{bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
A new admiral orders new sensors

New Admiral Gabe Nuer took the high ring, and the next day came an order: fit his tracking sensors or pay a heavy port fee. Only his cousin's firm sells them, through {bot1}'s berths, in blessed crates. {bot3} had its own sensors ready. Someone wants the whole market.
Report the scheme
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Ship upkeep rises clearly for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands sharply softer.
The scheme is reported

You sent the order, the price list and the cousin's name to the Bureau. It paid an informant's fee and froze half the refit berths for audit. Your ships stand in queues, so Ship upkeep rises for a while. {bot}'s next weather lands sharply softer: the scheme ran on its berths.
entries.place: MIL_B1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands sharply softer.
Fit the sensors
Get: Military volume up a little for the rest of the run. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the slips. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
The sensors are fitted

You paid for the sensors and fitted every ship. The admiral's lanes now list you as trusted, so your Military volume rises for the rest of the run. {bot}'s own sensors were turned away, and its next weather comes a little later. The new sensors hum a canticle no list names.
entries.place: MIL_B1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Inspector Voss queries a relay

Since your report, Inspector Kethra Voss audits every refit, her stamp worn like a sidearm. One relay in your batch bears the serial of a ship scrapped before your time. {bot2}'s parade squadrons carry it too, and {bot1}'s older fleets. Send it for review, or swap it and refile.
entries.place: MIL_B2 choice screen body after opt_a of MIL_B1

entries.text: Your fleet wears the admiral's sensors. Inspector Kethra Voss, her stamp worn like a sidearm, queries one relay: it bears the serial of a ship scrapped before your time. {bot2}'s parade squadrons carry it too, and {bot1}'s older fleets. Send it for review, or swap it and refile.
entries.place: MIL_B2 choice screen body after opt_b of MIL_B1

entries.text: Send the part for review
Get: Military price up a little for a while. Cost: one route's trip cost rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The office reviews the part

The relay went for review. Voss read your forms, then everyone's. {bot}, whose squadrons carry that relay, lost contracts, and its next weather lands a little softer. The cleared stamp lifts Military prices for a while. One route sat in customs, and its trip cost rises a little.
entries.place: MIL_B2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
Swap the part and refile
Get: {cash_in} credits for the old part. Cost: Military volume down a little for a few cycles. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The part is swapped

You swapped the relay and refiled. The old part sold for credits, still humming its dead ship's litany. Voss applied the same clause to {bot1}'s older fleets, which stood idle, so {bot}'s next weather lands a little softer. Ships waited, and Military volume dips for a few cycles.
entries.place: MIL_B2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands a little softer.
The Feast of Arms offers a stall

The relay review is done. Madame Orlenne Vaux, who runs the high-ring Feast of Arms, offers you a place. {bot3} keeps a stand there every year, always crowded. {bot2} holds a gala next door. Buy the main hall for the week, or take the east stand beside {bot3}'s.
entries.place: MIL_B3 choice screen body after opt_a of MIL_B2

entries.text: The inspector has ruled on the new relay. Madame Orlenne Vaux, who runs the high-ring Feast of Arms, offers you a place. {bot3} keeps a stand there every year, always crowded. {bot2} holds a gala next door. Buy the main hall for the week, or take the east stand beside {bot3}'s.
entries.place: MIL_B3 choice screen body after opt_b of MIL_B2

entries.text: Buy the main hall
Get: Military volume up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the main hall. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The main hall is yours

You bought the hall for the week, and it cost credits. Buyers walked past empty stands to reach yours, so your Military volume rises for a while. {bot} sold from the corridor, and its next weather lands clearly softer. The relic cannon, which fires blanks only, saluted you.
entries.place: MIL_B3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather lands clearly softer.
Take the east stand
Get: {n} units of tech progress. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the stand. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer, and all three houses' next weather comes a little later.
The east stand

You took the east stand beside {bot3}'s and paid on the day. Two engineers from the next stand talked shop, and tech progress came in. {bot2}, whose gala crowd walked past, gets a little softer weather, and all three houses, {bot} among them, send theirs a little later.
entries.place: MIL_B3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: All three houses: next weather comes a little later.
{bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
A Fleet Office clerk asks for terms

Your week in the main hall brought the fleets to you. A Fleet Office clerk asks you to set the terms of a supply agreement for many cycles, under an estimate that renews itself with the words until victory. Roster deliveries by garrison, or by week. {bot} watches from the door.
entries.place: MIL_B4 choice screen body after opt_a of MIL_B3

entries.text: Your days at the east stand brought the fleets to you. A Fleet Office clerk asks you to set the terms of a supply agreement for many cycles, under an estimate that renews itself with the words until victory. Roster deliveries by garrison, or by week. {bot} watches from the door.
entries.place: MIL_B4 choice screen body after opt_b of MIL_B3

entries.text: Roster by garrison
Get: Military price up a little for a while. Cost: Military volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
Rostered by garrison

Deliveries are rostered by garrison, each with its own price sheet and blessing. Military orders thinned for a while as the rosters were written, and the price of standing orders rose. {bot} had counted on the fleets as its client, and its next weather lands clearly softer.
entries.place: MIL_B4 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
Roster by week
Get: {cash_in} credits. Cost: Ship upkeep rises clearly for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer; {bot3}'s lands a little softer.
Rostered by week

Deliveries are rostered by week from your desk, and the fleets are held ready. A large payment arrived, and the clerk stamped the roster. Ships kept ready cost more, so Ship upkeep rises for a while. {bot}'s next weather lands clearly softer, and {bot3}'s lands a little softer.
entries.place: MIL_B4 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
A depot for Dunmere Reach

The Fleet Office has an estimate for Dunmere Reach, and a clerk at Cindrel needs a supplier before the next muster. {bot3} runs convoys on the same lane and bills by the hull. Keep a standing depot there, or ship to each muster as it is called.
Keep a standing depot
Get: Military volume up a little for a while. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
The depot is stocked

You leased a shed on Cindrel's dock and hired a night watch. Orders now come on a schedule, so Military volume rises for a while, and the watch raises Ship upkeep a little. {bot}'s convoys wait for slots at your door, and its next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: MIL_C1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Ship to each muster
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Military volume down a little for a few cycles. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer.
Mustered, one at a time

You shipped to each muster as it was called, and the clerk paid on the day. Your own orders dipped for a few cycles while the berth stood empty. {bot} had counted on the Fleet Office's steady custom, and its next weather lands a little softer.
entries.place: MIL_C1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
The inspector counts the halls

Your depot at Cindrel is stocked, and word of it reached the Bazaar. Inspector Kethra Voss comes to the new halls with her stamp worn like a sidearm. She will pass every door in one visit for a charge, or one by one on her own time. {bot1} has already paid.
entries.place: MIL_C2 choice screen body after opt_a of MIL_C1

entries.text: Your musters were paid, and word of it reached the Bazaar. Inspector Kethra Voss comes to the new halls with her stamp worn like a sidearm. She will pass every door in one visit for a charge, or one by one on her own time. {bot1} has already paid.
entries.place: MIL_C2 choice screen body after opt_b of MIL_C1

entries.text: Pay for one visit
Get: Military price up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the visit. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
Every door, one stamp

Voss passed every door in one visit and stamped the last as if it were a ruling. The visit cost credits, and Military price rises a little for a while. {bot} had paid first, and its next weather lands clearly softer.
entries.place: MIL_C2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
Wait door by door

Gekk hauled the whole stock away and paid on the dock. Your storage stood empty, and Minerals volume fell clearly for a few cycles. {bot}'s usual contract went with it, so its next weather lands sharply softer, and {bot3}'s lands a little softer. The racks rang as they emptied.
entries.place: MIN_B3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands sharply softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
Take a standing buyer
Get: Minerals volume up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits to the buyer's broker. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
A standing buyer signs

The standing buyer signed and sends a ship each cycle. Minerals volume rose for a while, and the buyer's broker was paid in credits. {bot} lost the buyer's custom, and its next weather lands clearly softer. The buyer's ship has no name on its hull.
entries.place: MIN_B3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
A new deposit is in range

You sold your whole ingot stock. Now a survey lists another deposit within reach of your ships, and {bot1} has already sent a charter crew. File the claim and pay the survey office, or lease the claim to a crew on terms.
entries.place: MIN_B4 choice screen body after opt_a of MIN_B3

entries.text: You took a standing buyer. Now a survey lists another deposit within reach of your ships, and {bot1} has already sent a charter crew. File the claim and pay the survey office, or lease the claim to a crew on terms.
entries.place: MIN_B4 choice screen body after opt_b of MIN_B3

entries.text: File the claim
Get: Minerals price up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits to the survey office for the filing. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands sharply softer.
The claim is filed

You filed the claim and the office stamped it. The filing cost credits, and Minerals prices rose a little for a while as your ore came to market. {bot}'s charter crew found your marker at the site, and its weather lands sharply softer. The deposit lay under the rock, unmoved.
entries.place: MIN_B4 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands sharply softer.
Lease the claim
Get: {cash_in} credits; Minerals volume up a little for the rest of the run. Cost: Ship upkeep up a little for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer; {bot3}'s a little softer.
The claim is leased

You leased the claim to a crew and the first payment arrived. Your ships carry its ore, so Minerals volume rose, and Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. {bot}'s weather lands clearly softer, and {bot3}'s a little softer: both lost the lease. It has a clause about weather.
entries.place: MIN_B4 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
Deepline Works wants a second shaft

The Deepline Works wants a second shaft sunk beside your claim at Cindrel, and needs a pump that only you can feed. {bot1} offers its own pump on lease, and {bot3} has asked for the spoil. Share your pump, or sell the Works the pump.
Share the pump
Get: Minerals volume up a little for a while. Cost: Minerals price down a little for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather comes a little later.
Two shafts, one pump

You shared the pump, and the Works sank its shaft beside yours. Minerals volume rises a little for a while, and more rock on the market pulls price down a little. {bot} had offered its own pump on lease, and its next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: MIN_C1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather comes a little later.
Sell the pump
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Minerals volume down a little for a few cycles. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The pump changes hands

You sold the pump, and the Works paid on the dock. Your own volume dipped for a few cycles while the shaft waited for a new crew. {bot} asked for the spoil and was told it was sold, and its next weather lands a little softer.
entries.place: MIN_C1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
Gordo Gekk prices the hall stone

Bidder Gordo Gekk, who says wanting more is only tidiness, has priced every slab in the Bazaar's new halls and wants yours. You shared your pump, so he calls you a friend. Fix one price for the run, or weigh each load as it comes. {bot1} supplies the rest.
entries.place: MIN_C2 choice screen body after opt_a of MIN_C1

entries.text: Bidder Gordo Gekk, who says wanting more is only tidiness, has priced every slab in the Bazaar's new halls and wants yours. You sold your pump, so he calls you a seller. Fix one price for the run, or weigh each load as it comes. {bot1} supplies the rest.
entries.place: MIN_C2 choice screen body after opt_b of MIN_C1

entries.text: Fix the slab price
Get: Minerals price up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the weighing seals. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands a little softer.
One price, tied with a bow

You fixed one price for every slab, and Gekk sealed it with a tidy bow. The weighing seals cost credits, and Minerals price rises a little for a while. {bot} supplies the rest of the halls, and its next weather lands a little softer.
entries.place: MIN_C2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands a little softer.
Weigh each load
Get: one route's trip cost down a little for a while. Cost: Minerals volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
Every load on the scale

You weighed each load as it came, and Gekk wrote down every figure and sighed at none. The busiest route's trip cost falls a little for a while, and Minerals volume dips as loads wait for the scale. {bot}'s next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: MIN_C2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Tamsk Reddock offers the last rail

The Great Hall wants rail for its roof. Tamsk Reddock, who runs the slag yard, offers you the whole of the last rail, and says heavy, as he does of everything. {bot1} wants the rest, and {bot3} wants the leftovers. Take the whole rail, or a share of it.
entries.place: MIN_C3 choice screen body after opt_a of MIN_C2

entries.text: The Great Hall wants rail for its roof. Tamsk Reddock, who runs the slag yard, saw your figures on the scale and offers you the whole of the last rail. He says heavy. {bot1} wants the rest, and {bot3} wants the leftovers. Take the whole rail, or a share of it.
entries.place: MIN_C3 choice screen body after opt_b of MIN_C2

entries.text: Take the whole rail
Get: Minerals volume up clearly for a while. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The whole rail

You took the whole last rail, and Reddock said heavy and meant it. Minerals volume rises clearly for a while, and the rail yard raises Ship upkeep a little. {bot} wanted the rest, and its next weather lands clearly softer.
entries.place: MIN_C3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
Take a share of it
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Minerals volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes clearly later.
A share of the rail

You took a share of the rail and the rest went to the yard. Credits came in at the dock, and Minerals volume dips for a while. {bot} wanted the leftovers and got them, and its next weather comes clearly later.
entries.place: MIN_C3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes clearly later.
A canister arrives unlabelled

A sealed canister reached your depot on Tillam from no named source. It is cold and damp, and the lid is warm. The label says: keep sealed, do not feed after dark. Director Hesk says the sample is fine. {bot2} asks to buy it unseen. Study it at your lab, or sell it as it came.
Study the sample
Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Culture Lab. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the tests. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather comes a little later.
The sample is studied

The lab worked behind two doors and logged every reading after dark. Tech progress came in, and the tests cost credits. {bot} had asked to buy the sample unseen, and its next weather comes a little later. Fitter Imre Fenn checked both doors twice. The vat took on a faint green.
entries.place: BIO_A1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather comes a little later.
Sell the sample
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Biotech price down a little for a few cycles. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The sample is sold

A broker took the canister the same day and paid cash. Buyers read the odd colour on the lid as a warning, so Biotech prices dip a little for a few cycles. {bot} was passed over, and its weather lands a little softer. Fenn asked where it went. The sample is fine, he was told.
entries.place: BIO_A1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
A clinic asks to test a batch

Your lab studied the sample. Now Doctor Marrow of the clinic ring asks to draw a batch from your stock for testing on her ward, where volunteers are volunteers by rota. {bot2} supplies the other wards, and {bot3} wants the data. Fund the clinic's tests, or run them at your lab.
entries.place: BIO_A2 choice screen body after opt_a of BIO_A1

entries.text: You sold the sample. Now Doctor Marrow of the clinic ring asks to draw a batch from your stock for testing on her ward, where volunteers are volunteers by rota. {bot2} supplies the other wards, and {bot3} wants the data. Fund the clinic's tests, or run them at your lab.
entries.place: BIO_A2 choice screen body after opt_b of BIO_A1

entries.text: Fund the clinic's tests
Get: Biotech volume up a little for the rest of the run. Cost: {cash_out} credits toward the tests. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
The clinic runs the tests

The clinic ran the tests behind its own doors. Your funding cost credits, and the clinic keeps ordering, so Biotech volume rises for the rest of the run. {bot} wanted the data and got a summary, so its weather comes a little later. The report came in triplicate, every copy damp.
entries.place: BIO_A2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Run the tests at your lab
Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Culture Lab. Cost: Biotech volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot2} {cut}.
The tests run at your lab

Your lab ran the tests on the held batch, and the vats gave tech progress. The batch left the shelves, so Biotech volume dips for a while. {bot} has its next weather held back as the clinic's wards moved to your results. Fenn walked the vat row each shift and wrote nothing down.
entries.place: BIO_A2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: {cut_std}.
A seal begins to weep

The clinic ran your tests. A vat seal at an Ashgate dock lab weeps. Director Hesk says the sample is fine. Fenn says the drop was clear at dawn and green by noon. {bot2} sources strains there, and {bot3} would buy the stock. Pause your lab for a check, or sell the stock.
entries.place: BIO_A3 choice screen body after opt_a of BIO_A2

entries.text: Your lab ran the tests. A vat seal at an Ashgate dock lab weeps. Director Hesk says the sample is fine. Fenn says the drop was clear at dawn and green by noon. {bot2} sources strains there, and {bot3} would buy the stock. Pause your lab for a check, or sell the stock.
entries.place: BIO_A3 choice screen body after opt_b of BIO_A2

entries.text: Pause the lab for a check
Get: Biotech price up a little for a while. Cost: the Culture Lab stands idle for a few cycles. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The lab is paused

You paused your lab and had every seal checked. Stock grew scarce, so Biotech prices rise a little for a while, and the lab stands idle for a few cycles. {bot}'s strains came from the weeping vat, and its weather lands a little softer. Fenn taped a note to the seal: told you.
entries.place: BIO_A3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
Sell the stock in that line
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Biotech volume down a little for a few cycles; {bot3}'s next weather lands a little harder. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The stock is sold

You sold the stock in that line and cash arrived. The shelves stood bare for a few cycles, so Biotech volume dips. {bot3} bought the surplus, so its weather lands a little harder, while {bot}'s lands clearly softer: its supply line came under notice. The vat moved at night.
entries.place: BIO_A3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands clearly softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little harder.
A hospital needs a rare strain

A hospital ring on Tillam needs a rare strain by cycle's end, and the cold chain is tight: warm crates mean lost cargo. {bot2} holds the stock, and {bot3} offers to carry it. The grower's manager says it is fine. Buy the stock, or culture it at your lab and send extra hulls.
Buy the grower's stock
Get: Biotech volume up clearly for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the grower's stock. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The stock is bought

You bought the grower's stock and shipped it as it was. It cost credits, and the hospital's order keeps your Biotech volume up for a while. {bot} held the only other stock, and its next weather lands clearly softer. One crate was warm at the dock. The manager said it was fine.
entries.place: BIO_B1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands clearly softer.
Culture it at your lab
Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Culture Lab. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The lab cultures the strain

Your lab grew the strain from a culture and the extra hulls carried it. Tech progress came in, and Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. {bot} offered to carry the order and was passed over, so its next weather lands a little softer. The strain came up a green nobody ordered.
entries.place: BIO_B1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
A strain changes in storage

You bought the grower's stock. One strain in storage has darkened, grows faster, and answers to the name on its crate. Cold-chain hand Ottoline Ryke says the lid was moved. {bot2} wants a sample, and {bot3} asks what it is worth. Relabel the batch, or sell it as a new line.
entries.place: BIO_B2 choice screen body after opt_a of BIO_B1

entries.text: You cultured the strain at your lab. One strain in storage has darkened, grows faster, and answers to the name on its crate. Cold-chain hand Ottoline Ryke says the lid was moved. {bot2} wants a sample, and {bot3} asks what it is worth. Relabel the batch, or sell it as a new line.
entries.place: BIO_B2 choice screen body after opt_b of BIO_B1

entries.text: Relabel the batch
Get: Biotech price up a little for a while. Cost: Biotech volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather comes clearly later.
The batch is relabelled

You relabelled the batch and held it for study. The new line fetches a little more for a while, and your own volume dips a little as stock stays back. {bot}'s sample requests were refused, so its weather comes clearly later. The storage manager moved his desk out of the room.
entries.place: BIO_B2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather comes clearly later.
Sell it as a new line
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while; {bot2}'s next weather lands a little harder. Weather: {bot3} {cut}.
Sold as a new line

You sold the batch as a new line for cash. Extra hulls raise Ship upkeep a little for a while. {bot2} bought a sample, so its weather lands a little harder, while {bot} has its weather held back, its old line undercut. The buyer asked for a second batch. Ryke asked for a lock.
entries.place: BIO_B2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: {cut_std}.
{bot2}: next weather lands a little harder.
An exchange offers a slot

You relabelled the batch. A culture exchange offers you a numbered slot for your output, with a seat at the call each cycle. Lots and porters are numbered alike. {bot2} holds the first slot, and {bot3} the second. List your output now, or buy a slot outright.
entries.place: BIO_B3 choice screen body after opt_a of BIO_B2

entries.text: You sold the batch as a new line. A culture exchange offers you a numbered slot for your output, with a seat at the call each cycle. Lots and porters are numbered alike. {bot2} holds the first slot, and {bot3} the second. List your output now, or buy a slot outright.
entries.place: BIO_B3 choice screen body after opt_b of BIO_B2

entries.text: List your output now
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Biotech volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands sharply softer; {bot3}'s comes clearly later.
The output is listed

Your output went on the exchange list and the first payment cleared. Fewer lots stayed for buyers, so volume dips for a while. {bot} lost its first slot's edge, and its next weather lands sharply softer, while {bot3}'s comes clearly later. Crates and porters bear slot numbers.
entries.place: BIO_B3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands sharply softer.
{bot3}: next weather comes clearly later.
Buy a slot outright
Get: Biotech volume up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the slot. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer, and {bot3}'s comes a little later.
A slot is bought

You bought a slot at the call and paid in credits. Your lots now sell on schedule, so Biotech volume rises for a while. {bot}'s next weather lands a little softer and {bot3}'s comes a little later, as the call split their buyers. The bell at the call is struck by hand, by number.
entries.place: BIO_B3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
{bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
A storage firm offers cold racks

Your output is listed on the exchange. A storage firm offers cold racks in a derelict hull moored to the dock, resealed and renamed Aisle. {bot2} keeps its stock there, and {bot3} rents beside it. Rent racks by the cycle, or sell the firm your first claim to the aisle.
entries.place: BIO_B4 choice screen body after opt_a of BIO_B3

entries.text: You hold a slot at the exchange call. A storage firm offers cold racks in a derelict hull moored to the dock, resealed and renamed Aisle. {bot2} keeps its stock there, and {bot3} rents beside it. Rent racks by the cycle, or sell the firm your first claim to the aisle.
entries.place: BIO_B4 choice screen body after opt_b of BIO_B3

entries.text: Rent racks by the cycle
Get: Biotech price up a little for a while. Cost: Biotech volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands sharply softer.
The racks are rented

You rented racks by the cycle, and your stock stayed cold in the old hull. Held stock lifts prices a little for a while, and volume dips as it waits. {bot} lost its place at the front, and its next weather lands sharply softer. The hull ticks as it cools. Ryke counts the doors.
entries.place: BIO_B4 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands sharply softer.
Sell the first claim
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s and {bot3}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The first claim is sold

You sold the firm your first claim to the aisle, and a large payment cleared. Your ships work new routes, so Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. {bot} and {bot3} both lost the aisle, and each sees its weather land clearly softer. One lamp lights the hull and does not flicker.
entries.place: BIO_B4 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2} and {bot3}: next weather lands clearly softer.
A chiller fails at Brannock

Ottoline Ryke calls from Brannock's grain dock. A chiller has failed and the racks are warming. Director Hesk says the samples are fine. Move your stock to the cold racks across the dock, or share her spare chiller. {bot2} stores there, and {bot3} rents beside it.
Move stock to cold racks
Get: Biotech price up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the racks. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The trays cross the dock

Ryke moved your trays to the racks across the dock and the warm alarm stopped. The racks cost credits, and Biotech price rises a little for a while. {bot} stores there too, and its next weather lands a little softer. Hesk said the samples were fine.
entries.place: BIO_C1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
Share her spare chiller
Get: Biotech volume up a little for a while. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
Two crews, one chiller

Ryke wheeled her spare chiller to your racks and the two crews shared the cold. Biotech volume rises a little for a while, and the extra crew raises Ship upkeep a little. {bot} rents beside the dock, and its next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: BIO_C1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Doctor Marrow volunteers again

Your racks held, and the Bazaar noticed. The new halls need a test rota, and Doctor Marrow, who volunteers by rota, has put his name on every line. Fund the whole rota, or count the samples yourself. {bot2} supplies strains, and {bot3} buys the stock.
entries.place: BIO_C2 choice screen body after opt_a of BIO_C1

entries.text: Your shared chiller hums, and the Bazaar noticed. The new halls need a test rota, and Doctor Marrow, who volunteers by rota, has put his name on every line. Fund the whole rota, or count the samples yourself. {bot2} supplies strains, and {bot3} buys the stock.
entries.place: BIO_C2 choice screen body after opt_b of BIO_C1

entries.text: Fund the whole rota
Get: one route's trip cost down a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the rota. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather comes a little later.
Marrow signs every line

You funded the rota, and Marrow signed up for every line of it. The rota cost credits, and the busiest route's trip cost falls a little for a while. {bot} supplies strains to the halls, and its next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: BIO_C2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather comes a little later.
Count the samples
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Biotech volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather lands a little softer.
Counted twice

You counted the samples yourself, twice, and Marrow stood by with a pen. Credits came in at the dock, and Biotech volume dips for a while as lots wait for the count. {bot} buys the stock, and its next weather lands a little softer.
entries.place: BIO_C2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
Director Hesk says it is fine

The last hall is roofed, and Director Hesk says again that the sample is fine. Imre Fenn, who fitted the seals, asks to read each one aloud before the cold rooms are sealed. {bot2} wants the rooms filled today, and {bot3} wants them listed.
entries.place: BIO_C3 choice screen body after opt_a of BIO_C2

entries.text: The last hall is roofed, and Director Hesk says again that the sample is fine. Imre Fenn, who fitted the seals, asks to read each one aloud before the cold rooms are sealed. {bot2} wants the rooms filled today, and {bot3} wants them listed. Your count is in the file.
entries.place: BIO_C3 choice screen body after opt_b of BIO_C2

entries.text: Seal the rooms today
Get: Biotech price up clearly for a while. Cost: Biotech volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The rooms are sealed

You sealed the rooms that day, and Hesk said the sample was fine, again. Biotech price rises clearly for a while, and the sealed rooms hold stock back, so volume dips a little. {bot} wanted the rooms filled, and its next weather lands clearly softer.
entries.place: BIO_C3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands clearly softer.
Read the seals aloud
Get: Biotech volume up clearly for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the extra shifts. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
Every seal, aloud

The crew read the seals aloud, one by one, with Fenn at the door. The extra shifts cost credits, and Biotech volume rises clearly for a while. {bot} wanted the rooms listed, and its next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: BIO_C3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: Perk
Marek Voss
Idris Kane
Sela Oru
Tamsin Hale

Marek kept ten ships flying on a shoestring and counts every bolt. He distrusts luck. He started his own company because nobody would let him order spare parts in bulk. He runs Minerals on a Tramp: one more lane beats one big hull.

Idris was a broker with a famous smile and a habit of buying lunch for rivals. He reads a price board the way others read faces. He spends freely and sells hard. He sells Luxury from a Dart: quick hops, a light hold, and the buyer still smiling.

Sela flew supply runs through the worst lanes of the rim and still came home. Bad news does not scare her, only an idle ship does. Her plans have a backup, and a backup for the backup. She runs Military on a Bulkhead. The rim taught her to fill the hold.

Tamsin grew up in the docking rings of the Bazaar and knows every clerk by name. Her contracts arrive with friendly paperwork and larger quantities. She is calm, and a little proud of the old place. She trades Biotech from a Skerrit, a hull she knows.
Old Contacts
Quick Read
Hard Lanes
Station Born
Bad events are announced one cycle early.
In the first cycle you see price tips on your home market.
Your first lane carries one step more cargo. Your Flagship can Boost a few times.
Contract orders ask for more units, so a filled order pays more.
Minerals: rock, every bolt counted

entries.text: More than half of Military now runs through you, and the Bureau has entered the company as supplier of record. The fleets you supply do not fire. They arrive, they are seen, and the quarrel at the border post ends by itself. The terms are posted and the ledgers can be read, which is dull, and works. Nobody in the Commons sleeps better, because nobody knows how close it was. Harrow Combine still runs its foundries, smaller and watching. The garrisons write you short letters that begin with thanks and end with a requisition.
entries.place: End screen body, win Military, good outcome

entries.text: The Lit Gallery
entries.place: End screen heading, win Luxury, good outcome

entries.text: More than half of Luxury moves through you, and the doors are wide. Silk and cut glimmers went where the Plan had never thought to send beauty: the dock mess, the night shift, the school on the ring. Masks that once cost a season's rations were lent at festivals and came back with a stain and a story. Velvet Concord still keeps the grand tables, though fewer people stand at them. The Bureau drafted a form for the allocation of beauty and then, to its credit, left it blank.
entries.place: End screen body, win Luxury, good outcome

entries.text: The Footing
entries.place: End screen heading, win Minerals, good outcome

entries.text: More than half of Minerals comes through you, and most of it went into ground. Ingot from the smelter, alloy from the deep cuts, plate from the fabric: the next ring of homes stands on them, with floors that do not ring when walked. The crews rotate on a posted schedule. Harrow Combine still cuts, at its own pace, in its own corner. The Bureau counted the new homes and found, to its surprise, that a form existed for them. Under the floors the stone is patient. It always was.
entries.place: End screen body, win Minerals, good outcome

entries.text: The Long Harvest
entries.place: End screen heading, win Biotech, good outcome

entries.text: More than half of Biotech passes through you, and it goes out the door. Bio-gel and gene seed reached the terraces at Tillam, the fields at Ashgate and clinics nobody had thought to supply. A cure went out on plain paper, with no licence number, and was copied by hand in rooms the Bureau never saw. Velvet Concord still sells the fine strains to those who can pay. The Plan took the credit, which is its way. In the culture lab the vats hum at the pace of something with all the time it needs.
entries.place: End screen body, win Biotech, good outcome

entries.text: The Full Racks
entries.place: End screen heading, win Military, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Military runs through you, and the fleets answer. Not to the Commons, and not to you exactly. They answer to the order book, and the order book answers to whoever paid last. The Bureau entered you as supplier of record and asked, very quietly, whether copies of the order forms might reach it first. They cannot. A border post has two flags now and one purchase order. You are never at the front. You only stand where the front is paid for. The racks are full and the cores hum. A great many people are armed, and the Plan has not yet decided what to call it.
entries.place: End screen body, win Military, bad outcome

entries.text: The Gilded Cage
entries.place: End screen heading, win Luxury, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Luxury is yours, and everyone wants what only you hold. Prices climb the way stairs do in a dream. Buyers who once haggled now wait, and the ones who cannot wait send guards. Your vaults are lit gold and built like a cell. The Bureau entered you as supplier of record and asked, politely, how many locks. Velvet Concord's masks hang in its empty halls. You hold everything the sky finds beautiful, and no one left may touch it unwatched. The cut glimmers hum faintly as you pass, the way glass does before it breaks.
entries.place: End screen body, win Luxury, bad outcome

entries.text: The Strip
entries.place: End screen heading, win Minerals, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Minerals comes through you, and the seams are paying for it. Cinderrest and Greywake were cut to the bone, and then to the bone beneath. White dust has reached the lamps of more rocks, and the Bureau lists every one as uninhabited. They are not. The crews work each cut to its rim until it is gone. Ingot, alloy and plate leave in long rows, and the dead worlds spread one cut at a time. Harrow Combine's crews drift off to other rock. The glass in the walls hums once, low, where it stopped being a wall.
entries.place: End screen body, win Minerals, bad outcome

entries.text: The Locked Seed
entries.place: End screen heading, win Biotech, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Biotech is yours, and the seed is locked. Gene seed leaves the culture lab under a seal and a ticket for every batch. The terraces at Tillam and the fields at Ashgate grow what you allow, on terms the Bureau calls reasonable. Nothing is withheld in anger. It is withheld by paperwork, which is quieter. Velvet Concord cannot sell what your wall will not let it copy. The vats are clean and the shelves are full. In the lab, something small and patented turns toward the light.
entries.place: End screen body, win Biotech, bad outcome

entries.text: The Ledger Closes
entries.place: End screen heading, no ship left and cash still negative (loss)

entries.text: The company has no ships left, and the cash is still below zero. Each cycle the Bureau took the newest hull to cover the debt, and now the last is gone. Your ships are entered in the Common Ledger, and your name is given a quota that is equal and exactly the size of everyone else's. A clerk reads the closing form aloud and adds that nothing here was ever owed to you. The three rivals go on selling. The sky did not notice.
entries.place: End screen body, no ship left and cash still negative (loss)

entries.text: Cycles taken
Final credits
This run is over. Start a new game or go to the main menu.
entries.place: End screen, above the buttons, every ending

entries.text: New game
Main menu
Quit game
The Standing Fleet kept every rival's growth held down to the last cycle. Nobody asked how.
You bought one rival's best client with a handshake and a gift. The guild filed it as courtesy.
The last seam in reach was yours, and the rivals worked the rest. They do not mention it.
The Patent Wall stands. The rivals' vats run slower behind it, and the clerks call that quality control.
The {workshop} never finished a tech. It ran on habit and steady hands.
entries.place: Epilogue 2, no tech done in the win market

entries.text: One tech came out of the {workshop}. It is mentioned in the minutes.
Two techs came out of the {workshop}. The third is still on the board.
All three techs came out of the {workshop}. The board has run out of things to approve.
{bot} lost a tier in Military and has not come back. Its letters are shorter now.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Military ({bot})

entries.text: {bot} lost a tier in Luxury. Its masks are still worn, by fewer faces.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Luxury ({bot})

entries.text: {bot} lost a tier in Minerals. Its crews cut the same rock, with less to show.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Minerals ({bot})

entries.text: {bot} lost a tier in Biotech. Its vats run on, and its clinics ask for less.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Biotech ({bot})

entries.text: The Unfinished Bazaar
entries.place: End screen heading, term ended before the Bazaar opened (soft ending)

entries.text: The term is over. The Bazaar is not open, and the Bureau has written that down without any word for it. You did not lose. The crew is paid, the ships are docked, and the worlds you grew are still lit. Someone has left a lamp on in the half-built hall. The Plan will start a new five cycles. The people on the stairs go on climbing them. They have time. So do you, if you want it.
entries.place: End screen body, term ended before the Bazaar opened (soft ending)

entries.text: No stage was finished. The ground is marked out, and the crew sits on it to eat.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, no stage done

entries.text: One stage stands. Children from the lower rings walk in and out of it.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, one stage done

entries.text: Two stages stand. The third is a frame, and in the evening the wind plays it.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, two stages done

entries.text: Only the last hall is missing. The roof has a gap, and the stars use it.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, three or more stages done

entries.text: {planet} keeps the site and keeps the lamp lit. Its people call it the Bazaar already.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, a capital was founded; {planet}

entries.text: At {planet} the lamps stay on past the hour. The Bureau opens a new page for it.
Lights burn on worlds that were dark when you came. Someone walks home along them.
The grey world has a green edge now. A child there asks what the red haze was.
entries.place: Epilogue, win, a dead world was reclaimed

entries.text: The Wing of Holds is full of crates. The Flagship sits low at its dock.
The Wing of Reach has a long window. From it, other systems look close.
The Wing of Tolls keeps a long desk and a short queue. Everyone is counted twice.
The Wing of Benches smells of hot metal. The night shift has its own kettle.
The Wing of Lamps has shutters for storms. When a storm comes, they stay open.
The Wing of Couriers has a bell for late arrivals. It rings more than it should.
The Long Shift
entries.place: End screen heading, Marek, many Restless cycles

entries.text: The Bazaar opened. On the worlds along the way, for a long while, the lights were low. Needs went unmet cycle after cycle, and people made do, because people do. Marek read every report. He did not look away from any of them. The doors are open now and the halls are full. Some of the faces in them remember the hungry cycles, and some of those faces are kind. Marek keeps the old reports in a drawer, and does not throw them out.
entries.place: End screen body, Marek, many Restless cycles

entries.text: Marek signs the opening page last. His hand does not shake. He holds the pen a little longer than he needs to.
Down the Seams
entries.place: End screen heading, Marek, mining platforms and a deep Minerals tree

entries.text: The grey worlds are working now. Platforms sit on rock that nobody listed as home, and the crews who run them sleep with the dust on their sleeves. Marek went down to see the first cut himself. He did not say much. He picked up a handful of the stone and put it back where it was. The Bazaar stands because of what came out of the dark. Someone has to remember that, and he does.
entries.place: End screen body, Marek, mining platforms and a deep Minerals tree

entries.text: A lamp burns on a platform nobody visits. The crew who keep it call it the porch.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Marek, platforms and a deep Minerals tree

entries.text: The Man Who Picked Up
entries.place: End screen heading, Marek, many signals and salvage answered

entries.text: When the call came, Marek answered. A signal out of the dark past Ashgate, a drifting pod off Tillam, a voice asking only once. He did not always have the fuel for it. He found the fuel. The Bazaar opened on a long list of small yeses. Nobody will carve them into a wall. The ones who were answered will remember, which is how a name lasts here. The old yard man sends a note. It has one line. It says, you picked up.
entries.place: End screen body, Marek, many signals and salvage answered

entries.text: Every signal on the board has the same reply scratched under it, in Marek's hand. It says, on its way.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Marek, many signals and salvage answered

entries.text: The Thin Fleet
entries.place: End screen heading, Marek, a small fleet

entries.text: You won with fewer hulls than anyone thought it could take. Every ship ran full and came home. Nothing sat at a dock, eating upkeep. The crew ate at one table all the way, and the table never grew too big to pass the bread. Marek calls it arithmetic. The crew calls it being looked after. The Bureau notes that the fleet is small and asks, politely, whether more is planned. It is not.
entries.place: End screen body, Marek, a small fleet

entries.text: The ships are few and well used. Each has a name the crew can say without looking.
Everyone Knows the Smile
entries.place: End screen heading, Idris, many worlds reached, LUX_1 learned

entries.text: Idris did not sell to one world. He sold to all of them, a little at a time, and each one told the next. By the day the Bazaar opened, a dock clerk on the farthest post knew the smile and had never seen it. Doors opened wherever your ships landed. Idris takes the credit for the smile and none for the luck. He stands in the doorway and shakes every hand, because someone made the trip.
entries.place: End screen body, Idris, many worlds reached, LUX_1 learned

entries.text: Letters come from posts you never saw. Most say only that the writer heard the name and wanted to say hello.
A Hull for Every Guest
entries.place: End screen heading, Idris, a large fleet

entries.text: The hangar is loud. Ships come and go all day, one for each lane, and Idris greets every pilot by name. The fleet was never cheap to keep. Ship upkeep was a weight the crew felt on every payday. But the lanes ran, and a world that waits for a ship forgives a lot. At the Opening Idris stood on the dock and counted the hulls. He lost count, and was glad.
entries.place: End screen body, Idris, a large fleet

entries.text: Pilots pass in the corridor and nod at each other. It is the sound of a company that is never alone.
A Seat Always Free
entries.place: End screen heading, Idris, signals and salvage answered, few missed

entries.text: Nothing sat unanswered on the board. Every signal found a ship, and every pod found a dock. Those who called learned that when Idris said yes, someone came, and they stopped asking twice. One table at the Bazaar stays empty at the end of the night. It is kept for whoever needs a good by morning. Idris does not call it a plan. He calls it manners.
entries.place: End screen body, Idris, signals and salvage answered, few missed

entries.text: The empty table has a card on it. The card is blank on purpose, and someone fills it in each morning.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Idris, signals and salvage answered, few missed

entries.text: The Corner Table
entries.place: End screen heading, Idris, few worlds, known well

entries.text: You kept to a few worlds, and you knew each one well. Idris read their boards like faces and sold to them as if each buyer were his only guest. The Bazaar stands on those few worlds, and they hold it up. The far posts never heard the name. Maybe that is the cost. Idris does not mind. He has a corner table, a clear view of the door, and a smile that never wore thin.
entries.place: End screen body, Idris, few worlds, known well

entries.text: Three docks know his name, and each has kept a chair. He has not yet sat in all of them.
The Hull She Lost
entries.place: End screen heading, Sela, a ship was repossessed

entries.text: A ship was taken, and the crew felt the dock go quiet. Sela went to see the empty berth herself. She did not look away. The Bureau took what the debt asked, in its slow polite way, and left the rest. You rebuilt from what was left. The Bazaar opened with fewer hulls than the plan. The berth is still empty. Someone leaves a lamp there, and Sela does not ask who.
entries.place: End screen body, Sela, a ship was repossessed

entries.text: She still checks the empty berth before every long flight. The lamp is always lit.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Sela, a ship was repossessed

entries.text: No Hull Sat Still
entries.place: End screen heading, Sela, signals and salvage answered, few missed

entries.text: Not one signal faded on the board. Not one hull waited for a stamp it could have bought. Sela flew the worst lanes in the rim, and she learned there what a ship costs when it stands still. Now every ship moves. The Bazaar opened on time, and for once nobody checked the sky for what was coming. Sela did, from habit. She stood at the window until the last hull left the dock. Then she sat down.
entries.place: End screen body, Sela, signals and salvage answered, few missed

entries.text: The dock bell rings for a departure, not an arrival. Sela says it is the only bell worth a thought.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Sela, signals and salvage answered, few missed

entries.text: The Long Way Round
entries.place: End screen heading, Sela, many worlds explored and settled

entries.text: The hard lanes were the ones nobody else would fly, and you flew them. The Flagship went out into the dark and came back with names. You put posts on worlds that were only a shape in the glass. Sela knew the cold out there. She did not say it was fine. She said it was worth knowing. Now the map is full of lit places that were black. Each one has a ship docked, and a crew that chose it.
entries.place: End screen body, Sela, many worlds explored and settled

entries.text: On the chart, the first dark world you lit has a small ring drawn round it in her pencil.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Sela, many worlds explored and settled

entries.text: The Night Watch
entries.place: End screen heading, Sela, a large fleet and calm worlds

entries.text: A big fleet, and every world fed. It should have been chaos, and it was not. Sela ran the lanes like a watch: each ship on its hour, each world on its list. She slept in her chair most nights. At the Opening she took the late watch alone, as she always has, and no ship called for her. She stayed anyway. It was the first quiet night she had ever owned.
entries.place: End screen body, Sela, a large fleet and calm worlds

entries.text: The radio is silent. Sela leaves it on, and turns the chair a little toward it.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Sela, a large fleet and calm worlds

entries.text: Still Writing Back
entries.place: End screen heading, Tamsin, many Restless cycles

entries.text: The Bazaar opened, and on some worlds the lights had been low for a long time. Tamsin knew the clerks there. She had their cards. She read each hungry report and wrote back a line, by hand. It did not fill a hold. It did not hurt either, and it was all she had on the nights the lanes failed. The halls are full now. She still writes back. Some of the clerks write to her first.
entries.place: End screen body, Tamsin, many Restless cycles

entries.text: A stack of old reports sits by her bed. She reads one before sleep, as other people read a letter.
The Ring Grows Up
entries.place: End screen heading, Tamsin, worlds grown to cities

entries.text: The world you raised from a quiet dock is a city now. Tamsin walked its halls on the opening night and knew the clerks by their steps. The paperwork is friendly and the lines are short. People who were children on the stairs run the desks. She sends a card to every one. The Bazaar stands on a world that was once small enough to know by heart. She still does. It is the same world, and louder.
entries.place: End screen body, Tamsin, worlds grown to cities

entries.text: Someone has painted the old dock number on the wall of the new hall, small, by the door.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Tamsin, worlds grown to cities

entries.text: Every Clerk Has a Card
entries.place: End screen heading, Tamsin, many worlds with a warm face

entries.text: Warm faces greet you at the docks. Tamsin knew the clerks, and they knew her. When a form had a flaw, a kind word fixed it. When a world ran short, someone called her first. It is not a plan the Bureau can file. It is a habit of being decent, and it carried you further than a good price would. At the Opening a dozen cards arrive by hand. Tamsin reads every name.
entries.place: End screen body, Tamsin, many worlds with a warm face

entries.text: The cards are pinned to a board by the door. A new one is added most days, and none is taken down.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Tamsin, many worlds with a warm face

entries.text: The Shelf Is Full
entries.place: End screen heading, Tamsin, Space Storage used throughout

entries.text: The shelves never ran bare. Food sat in the Space Storage through the lean cycles, held for the day a world asked. Tamsin counted the stock every night, and slept better for it. Some called it hoarding. The terraces that were fed from it did not. When the Bazaar opened there was still a full shelf at the back, and a note on it. The note says, for whoever is next.
entries.place: End screen body, Tamsin, Space Storage used throughout

entries.text: The note on the shelf is in her hand. Underneath, in another hand, someone has written, thank you.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Tamsin, Space Storage used throughout

entries.text: Done by Hand
entries.place: End screen heading, Tamsin, routes set from the planet card

entries.text: Every route was set by hand, at the planet card, with the page open and the numbers read aloud. Tamsin never trusted a lane she had not looked at. It was slower. It was also right more often than not, and when it was wrong she knew why. The Bazaar opened on lanes she can name from memory, in the order she laid them. She runs a finger down the list on the wall. It is the nearest thing to a map she has ever drawn.
entries.place: End screen body, Tamsin, routes set from the planet card

entries.text: The list on the wall is in pencil. She has never once rubbed a line out.
entries.place: Epilogue 1, Tamsin, routes set from the planet card

entries.text: The halls are warm, and the stone under them held. Marek stands on it a while and lets himself be glad.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Minerals (Marek Voss) CEO ending, world turned out kind

entries.text: The halls are loud and the seams are bare. Marek counts what the rock gave, and what it was never asked for.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Minerals (Marek Voss) CEO ending, world turned out cold

entries.text: Doors open before the ships land. Idris says the sky is kind, and for once he is not selling anything.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Luxury (Idris Kane) CEO ending, world turned out kind

entries.text: The smile is still on every door, but the welcome has gone cold. Idris notices who stopped saying his name.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Luxury (Idris Kane) CEO ending, world turned out cold

entries.text: The border is quiet and the dock is warm. Sela lets her shoulders drop one inch, where nobody sees.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Military (Sela Oru) CEO ending, world turned out kind

entries.text: The racks are full and the quiet is a held breath. Sela keeps her coat on indoors.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Military (Sela Oru) CEO ending, world turned out cold

entries.text: The terraces answer when Tamsin calls. Every card that comes back has a warm word on it.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Biotech (Tamsin Hale) CEO ending, world turned out kind

entries.text: The cards come back short and formal. Tamsin reads them twice and cannot find herself in them.
entries.place: Epilogue, win with a Biotech (Tamsin Hale) CEO ending, world turned out cold

entries.text:
A clinic worker lays a sheet beside the charter crate. The Star Bazaar's lamps are lit. Tamsin holds the paper flat while the worker finds a pen.

It is the cure, copied by hand. There is no licence number. Medicine and gene seed have reached terraces, fields, and clinics beyond the usual lists.

Across the hall, Velvet Concord's fine strains wait behind glass. A Bureau clerk slowly writes the Plan's name above the harvest. Tamsin keeps her palm on the sheet.
entries.place: End screen, The Long Harvest scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
The clinic worker finishes a copy and passes it across. Someone else pulls a sheet of plain paper from a bag. From the culture lab comes the slow hum of the vats.

Tamsin moves her hand so they can use the table. The charter crate is empty beside them. The cure goes out folded small enough for a pocket.
entries.place: End screen, The Long Harvest scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
By the lab counter, a grower holds an empty seed tray. The Star Bazaar's lamps have come on. Tamsin smooths a folded ticket against the counter.

Inside the culture lab, sealed batches fill the shelves. Each needs its own ticket before it can leave. The Bureau clerk checks the grower's form, slowly and without a frown.

Velvet Concord has sent a request to copy a strain. It rests under the same glass as the grower's ticket. A shoot with a patent tag bends toward the lamp.
entries.place: End screen, The Locked Seed scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
The clerk slides the ticket back. "Please bring the matching copy." The grower looks from the stamp to the sealed shelf.

The clerk turns to the next form. Tamsin is still holding the returned ticket. The grower shifts the empty tray to the other arm.
entries.place: End screen, The Locked Seed scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
