A dock clerk brings an envelope into the Great Hall. People pass with plates from the opening table. The clerk waits beside Tamsin's chair, holding the envelope by its edges.

Tamsin sets the opening page aside. There are old shortfall reports beneath it, kept in the order they came. She knows the clerk's hand before she reads the name.

The clerk pulls a chair close enough to share the desk. Tamsin uncaps her pen.
entries.place: End screen, Still Writing Back scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
The envelope holds a hungry report and a line asking after her. Tamsin reads the report again before she answers. The plates keep passing behind the clerk.

She writes a line by hand. The clerk waits for the ink, then folds the page to fit a pocket. The old reports stay beside her chair.
entries.place: End screen, Still Writing Back scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
In the city you helped grow, Tamsin stops beside some old paint. The dock mark is still there, low on the wall. A clerk catches her looking and rests a hand over it.

Tamsin knows that hand. Its owner used to sit on the stairs with schoolwork. Now the clerk runs the desk, and the queue is short.

People have come from the rings to mark the Bazaar's opening. The clerk has left a space for her card by the desk. Beyond it, the new hall fills with voices.
entries.place: End screen, The Ring Grows Up scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
Tamsin writes the clerk's name on a card and fills the waiting space. Before she goes, she touches the old paint with a fingertip. The clerk is already calling the next name.

She takes the turn toward the stairs without asking. Her hand finds the old rail before she looks down.
entries.place: End screen, The Ring Grows Up scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
A courier sets a packet of cards on Tamsin's chair. The Star Bazaar's guests are waiting along the wall. She loosens the thread without sitting down.

She knows the clerks' writing. They have sent word about short stock and caught flaws in her forms. The top card asks her to visit without an order to place.

There is a bare board by the hall's entrance. The courier holds up the packet, then looks at the board. Tamsin asks for pins.
entries.place: End screen, Every Clerk Has a Card scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
She reads each name before pressing a pin through its card. The courier reaches for the loose thread.

Tamsin takes the thread and slips it into her pocket. There is room on the board for the next card.
entries.place: End screen, Every Clerk Has a Card scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
At the back of Space Storage, Tamsin checks the food shelf. Music from the Bazaar's opening reaches the stock desk. A storage hand waits with Tamsin's coat over an arm.

The shelf is full. It held food through the lean stretches, when calls came from the terraces. Some called the stock hoarding. The terrace crews sent back the empty crates.

A note in Tamsin's hand hangs from the edge. It says, for whoever is next. There is a new line below it.
entries.place: End screen, The Shelf Is Full scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
The storage hand points to the new line. It says, thank you. Tamsin holds the paper steady with her thumb.

She closes the stock book and takes her coat. The note stays where a hand reaching for food will find it.
entries.place: End screen, The Shelf Is Full scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
The Bureau clerk asks for a route map. Tamsin points to the pencil list beside the Star Bazaar's loading desk. The clerk takes a seat and turns a clean page.

She kept each planet card open as she set its route. Someone read the stock aloud. If a lane failed, she wrote why beside it. No line has been rubbed out.

The opening crowd passes behind them. Tamsin puts a finger at the top of the list. The clerk waits for her to begin.
entries.place: End screen, Done by Hand scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
Tamsin names the lanes in the order she laid them. Her finger pauses where a note crowds the margin. The clerk asks whether to copy the notes as well.

"All of it," Tamsin says. She holds the list flat while the clerk writes. Her finger waits beside the next lane.
entries.place: End screen, Done by Hand scene close; no placeholders

entries.text: The Star Bazaar stands in {system}, raised through all {m} stages in {cycles} cycles. Tamsin kept the builders' cards from Foundations, Halls, Towers, and Great Hall. Each bears a name she can put to a face.
entries.place: End screen beat, completed Bazaar; {system} system name, {m} stages, {cycles} elapsed cycles

entries.text: In {system}, you founded the Star Bazaar and completed {n} of its {m} stages. Tamsin kept the cards from the crews who worked there. Their unfinished lists still have names beside each job.
entries.place: End screen beat, partly built Bazaar; {system} system name, {n} stages completed, {m} total stages

entries.text: You founded the Star Bazaar in {system}. None of its {m} stages was completed. Tamsin left space on the work sheet for the building crew's names.
entries.place: End screen beat, founded Bazaar with no completed stage; {system} system name, {m} total stages

entries.text: You never founded the Star Bazaar. Tamsin carried a blank site card among her clerk cards. Its corners softened with the others.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bazaar never founded; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Holds gave the Flagship a larger hold. A crew packing food could leave fewer crates on the dock. Tamsin checked the new limit before changing her load sheet.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Holds chosen, larger Flagship hold; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Reach let hubs serve worlds farther away. More dock clerks could put their needs on the same desk. Tamsin kept the distant cards beside the near ones.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Reach chosen, farther hub reach; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Tolls made your worlds pay more tax. Its clerks counted the larger sums into your income. Tamsin read the receipts with the worlds' requests beside them.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Tolls chosen, higher world tax; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Benches made new workshops cost less to build. A workshop crew could get its work space for fewer credits. Tamsin folded the new price sheet to fit behind her clerk cards.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Benches chosen, lower workshop build costs; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Lamps gave the Flagship a larger hold. More food or lab stock could travel in the same load. Tamsin marked the larger limit where the loading crew could read it.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Lamps chosen, larger Flagship hold; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Couriers raised the tax paid by your worlds. A clerk carried each larger count up the stair to the Bureau. Tamsin checked which world each payment came from before filing it.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Couriers chosen, higher world tax; no placeholders

entries.text: {names} remains an Outpost. Its clerk can call the whole dock crew without using the board. Tamsin's card hangs where a shift hand can reach it.
entries.place: End screen beat, world still at Outpost tier; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: On {n} worlds, the tier card still reads Outpost. The dock clerks know whose cup is missing from the mess. Tamsin leaves their requests beside the larger orders.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds still at Outpost tier; {n} worlds

entries.text: Your trade helped {names} become a Village. Families live beside the growing beds now. A shift hand can wave to a child at a window on the walk back.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to Village tier; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: With your trade, {names} grew into {n} Villages. Homes stand beyond the loading yards. Parents coming off shift have someone to wave to at a window.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Village tier; {names} is a ready plural list, {n} worlds

entries.text: Your shipments helped {names} grow into a Town. A clinic worker can finish a shift and buy supper on the way home. The clinic clerk has a desk away from the loading bench.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to Town tier; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} became {n} Towns through the trade you brought. There are streets between their homes, clinics, and market stalls. The clerks need longer address books when they write to Tamsin.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Town tier; {names} is a ready plural list, {n} worlds

entries.text: You helped {names} grow into a City. People who once waited with their parents now run the supply desks. Tamsin's cards reach clerks she remembers standing on chairs to see the counter.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to City tier; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} grew into {n} Cities with your trade. Their desk crews include people who learned their letters on old cargo slips. Tamsin has to ask which desk when a familiar voice calls.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to City tier; {names} is a ready plural list, {n} worlds

entries.text: {names} became a Metropolis, fed by the trade you brought. People travel between home and work without passing the old dock. Tamsin still sends her cards there, addressed to the clerk behind the old counter.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to Metropolis tier; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} became {n} Metropolises through your trade. Whole shifts live far from the docks that brought their families. A clerk can know a district by heart and never see the whole city. Tamsin still asks after the old dock mess.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Metropolis tier; {names} is a ready plural list, {n} worlds

entries.text: No world grew through your trade. Tamsin's clerk cards still carried the old addresses. There was no new street to write below them.
entries.place: End screen beat, no world grew; no placeholders

entries.text: Your supplies made {names} a living world again. The mining stopped there. People could tend growing beds instead of drawing stock from the cut. Tamsin copied "trading post" over the old platform address.
entries.place: End screen beat, dead world reclaimed; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are living worlds again, {n} places reclaimed with your supplies. Their mining stopped, and crews began tending beds beside the old work paths. Tamsin needed new cards for people who had come to stay.
entries.place: End screen beat, dead worlds reclaimed; {names} is a ready plural list, {n} worlds

entries.text: The Flagship built a post or platform for your company. A clerk stayed to keep the stock sheets. Tamsin wrote back until she knew that hand without the name.
entries.place: End screen beat, Flagship built a trading post or mining platform; no placeholders

entries.text: The Flagship built {n} trading posts and mining platforms. Each needed hands to check stock and keep the papers dry. Tamsin's card box grew heavier with their clerks' names.
entries.place: End screen beat, Flagship built trading posts and mining platforms; {n} combined total

entries.text: Your company reached {n} systems. Tamsin could no longer keep every clerk's working hours in her head. She marked them on the cards before making a call.
entries.place: End screen beat, systems reached; {n} systems

entries.text: Your fleet never grew beyond a {ship} hull. Its crew's names fitted on the back of Tamsin's card. She left room beside them for the loading shift.
entries.place: End screen beat, largest fleet had a single ship; {ship} is the singular ship type name

entries.text: At its largest, your fleet held {n} {ship} hulls. Each had hands expecting stock sheets and a place in the loading queue. Tamsin learned to match a pilot's writing to a hull.
entries.place: End screen beat, largest fleet; {n} ships, {ship} is the singular ship type name

entries.text: You started a route. Tamsin wrote its goods beside the receiving clerk's name. The crew could look at her page and know who would count the load.
entries.place: End screen beat, route started; no placeholders

entries.text: You started {n} routes. Tamsin kept the receiving clerks' names beside the goods on each line. A tired loader could find a contact without waking her.
entries.place: End screen beat, routes started; {n} routes

entries.text: You removed a route. Tamsin marked the change beside its old line. She waited while the loading clerk read it back.
entries.place: End screen beat, route removed, follows routes beat; no placeholders

entries.text: You removed {n} routes. Tamsin kept the old lines and wrote each change beside them. Loading clerks had to know which instructions no longer held.
entries.place: End screen beat, routes removed, follows routes beat; {n} routes

entries.text: Your people learned a new skill. Tamsin asked for the steps in plain words. A tired hand on the next shift would have to use them.
entries.place: End screen beat, skill learned; no placeholders

entries.text: Your people learned {n} skills. Tamsin kept notes where the next shift could find them. The marks grew uneven when someone stayed late to finish a page.
entries.place: End screen beat, skills learned; {n} skills

entries.text: You built a place for making goods or passing stock on. Tamsin wrote the shift contact inside its stock book. A tired hand could find a name before reaching for the radio.
entries.place: End screen beat, a workshop, the Fabric, or a hub built; no placeholders

entries.text: You built {n} places to make goods or pass stock on. Each needed stock sheets and someone to answer the radio. Tamsin kept a shift contact inside the cover of each book.
entries.place: End screen beat, workshops, the Fabric, and hubs built; {n} combined total

entries.text: The Flagship answered a signal. Tamsin asked what the crew found before she asked what they brought back. She left their account beside the job's payment line.
entries.place: End screen beat, signal answered by the Flagship; no placeholders

entries.text: The Flagship answered {n} signals. Your crew reached the places those calls came from. Tamsin kept their accounts with the job papers, even when there was no payment to enter.
entries.place: End screen beat, signals answered by the Flagship; {n} signals

entries.text: A signal went quiet before the Flagship answered it. Tamsin kept the call with the job papers. The space for a reply stayed blank.
entries.place: End screen beat, signal went quiet unanswered; no placeholders

entries.text: {n} signals went quiet without an answer from the Flagship. Tamsin copied their calls onto a sheet she kept outside the closed jobs. She could not fill in the reply column.
entries.place: End screen beat, signals went quiet unanswered; {n} signals

entries.text: A world ended a cycle without what it needed. Its clerk sent the shortfall on the usual sheet. Tamsin read past the total to the line asking when more could come.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world ended a cycle with an unmet need; no placeholders

entries.text: {n} times, a world ended a cycle short of what it needed. A clerk had to count the missing stock for people waiting below. Tamsin kept those reports even after the sheets grew soft at the fold.
entries.place: End screen beat, unmet needs counted per world per cycle; {n} occurrences, not elapsed cycles

entries.text: Relief credits kept the company going when it could not carry itself. Tamsin signed the receipt at the Bureau desk. The clerk checked the company name slowly, though they had known each other for years.
entries.place: End screen beat, relief credits kept the company alive; no placeholders

entries.text: Relief credits kept the company alive {n} times. Tamsin went back to the Bureau with the papers. The clerk offered her the same chair and checked each receipt slowly.
entries.place: End screen beat, relief credits kept the company alive; {n} payments

entries.text: The Bureau repossessed a ship for debt. Its clerk asked the crew to take their time. Tamsin took the shift card from the hull's file and kept it with her own.
entries.place: End screen beat, ship repossessed by the Bureau for debt; no placeholders

entries.text: The Bureau repossessed {n} ships for debt. The clerks waited while the crews took their things ashore. Tamsin kept the crew cards after the hull files passed across the desk.
entries.place: End screen beat, ships repossessed by the Bureau for debt; {n} ships

entries.text: Tamsin kept these moments beside the names of the people who had to live with them.
entries.place: End screen beat, single sentence before the game's list of decisive moments; no placeholders

entries.text: The terrace clerks answer when Tamsin calls. Their cards ask after her before listing the stock. She smooths each card flat before putting it away.
entries.place: End screen beat, warm world response before the scene close on a win; no placeholders

entries.text: The cards still come back, with stock lists and the right stamps. They address Tamsin by her full name. She runs her finger down a margin where there used to be a note.
entries.place: End screen beat, cold world response before the scene close on a win; no placeholders

entries.text:
The Bureau's notice lies on the control post table. The term is over. The Star Bazaar has not opened.

{ceo} sets the work record of {company} beside the notice. The crew has been paid. They sit down in their work coats. Someone shifts a cup to make room for the page.

You draw your chair closer. Someone holds the page flat while you read.
entries.place: End screen, term ended before the Bazaar opened; {company}, {ceo} is the CEO's full name; no Bazaar site assumed

entries.text:
The hand lifts from the page. {ceo} reaches for the cover, then leaves the book open. You put the Bureau's notice under the cup.

Beyond the glass, the dock lamps still burn. The next shift comes in with coats over their arms. You pull up a chair for them.
entries.place: End screen, after any subset of CEO beats for the unfinished ending; {ceo} is the CEO's full name

entries.text:
The Bureau clerk sets the ledger on a square of felt. {ceo} sits beside you at the desk. The clerk reads the name {company} and waits for you to nod.

Each cycle, the Bureau took the newest hull. The fleet is gone, and the company still owes credits. The ships are listed in the Common Ledger now.

The clerk lays the last form beside the book. Before you sign, the record of the company's work must be read. The clerk smooths the page and begins.
entries.place: End screen, no fleet ships left and credits still negative; {company}, {ceo} is the CEO's full name

entries.text:
The clerk turns the form toward you. Your new quota is the same as everyone else's. The clerk reads the line that says nothing was owed to you. Then the pen is set within reach.

You sign. {ceo} holds your copy flat while the ink dries. The clerk sets the closed ledger back on its square of felt. Beyond the glass, the freight lights keep their pace.
entries.place: End screen, after any subset of CEO beats, the last bankruptcy form is signed; {ceo} is the CEO's full name

entries.text:
A child stands beneath the gallery lamps, holding a festival mask. There is a food stain on its silk tie. Idris kneels to look.

The Star Bazaar has taken in the charter cargo. Its bright cloth is still spread beside the crate. Dock cooks browse the display tables beside teachers. Their work bags rest against the table legs.

A Bureau clerk waits with a form for lending beautiful things. The line for who may borrow them is blank. The child holds the mask out.
entries.place: End screen, The Lit Gallery, opening; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
Idris takes the mask and rubs the stain with his thumb. It stays.

The clerk asks who should be allowed to borrow it. Idris looks at the child. The child has already reached for it again.

He hands it back. The clerk folds the blank form and puts the pen away.
entries.place: End screen, The Lit Gallery, closing; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
The vault guard asks Idris to hold out his hands. Behind the glass, gems catch the gold light. The guard knows his face. The check takes its time.

A buyer waits outside with a price slip. There are crossed-out prices beneath the latest line. Their own guard waits on the stair. These pieces cannot be bought elsewhere.

The Star Bazaar is open. A Bureau clerk has come to list the locks. Idris smiles and waits for the vault guard to let him pass.
entries.place: End screen, The Gilded Cage, opening; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
The vault guard steps aside. Idris walks between the cases, his hands held clear of the glass.

The clerk asks, very gently, whether the list includes the inner lock. Idris turns. The vault guard has followed him in.

Outside, the buyer presses the price slip flat against the pane. Idris lowers his empty hands.
entries.place: End screen, The Gilded Cage, closing; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
The guest brings a folded list to the Star Bazaar. Idris meets them on the step.

They say his name before he gives it. At their far trading post, people knew the smile from other people's stories. Their clerk has sent them to meet it.

Behind them, the charter cloth lies beside its broken seal. Voices from other posts cross the hall. Idris holds out his hand. The guest moves the list so they can take it.
entries.place: End screen, Everyone Knows the Smile, opening; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
The guest unfolds the list. Idris lets the next hand wait while he reads the world names.

"Which dock?" he asks.

The guest points. Idris pulls a chair onto the step for them. He stays beside it, greeting each person who made the trip.
entries.place: End screen, Everyone Knows the Smile, closing; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
Idris has taken a piece of chalk to the hangar rail. Each passing hull gets a mark. The pay clerk leans beside him, holding the ship upkeep sheet.

The Star Bazaar is taking guests. A pilot crosses the hangar still wearing flight gloves. Idris greets them by name, then turns back to the glass.

Engines sound through the rail beneath his hand. The chalk hovers above a mark he may have made already.
entries.place: End screen, A Hull for Every Guest, opening; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
Idris has lost his place in the count. He wipes the chalk on his coat and gives the pilot his hand.

Beyond the glass, hulls pass on the lanes. He leaves the marks unfinished. He knows the names coming over the radio.
entries.place: End screen, A Hull for Every Guest, closing; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
A server sets a blank card on a table at the Bazaar. Idris turns it so it faces the room.

Guests have come with old signal slips in their pockets. Some brought parcels. Others brought nothing they could sell. Idris makes room for their coats.

The server asks whose table this is. Idris draws the spare chair back, but does not sit.
entries.place: End screen, A Seat Always Free, opening; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
A guest stops beside the blank card. "I need a cargo by morning," they say. The server reaches for a pen.

Idris lays a hand on the chair. "Sit while you tell us."

The guest takes off their coat. Idris slides the card across for them to write their name.
entries.place: End screen, A Seat Always Free, closing; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
The table is tucked into a corner of the Star Bazaar. From his chair, Idris can see each guest arrive.

A dock clerk has brought a board from home. Its edges are worn where Idris used to rest his hands. The clerk lays it beside his plate and waits.

There are few world names on it. Idris has bought lunch for people at each of them. The clerk taps a line with a finger.
entries.place: End screen, The Corner Table, opening; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text:
Idris reads the line the clerk is pointing to. Then he asks after the person who wrote it.

At the far posts, clerks still ask how to spell his name. Here, the server sets down his usual meal without asking.

He moves his plate aside so the clerk can sit.
entries.place: End screen, The Corner Table, closing; {company} and {ceo} optional

entries.text: In {system}, your Star Bazaar is built. Your crews raised all {m} stages in {cycles} cycles. They laid the Foundations, built the Halls and Towers, and roofed the Great Hall. A loader sets a silk parcel on a counter once marked only in chalk.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, completed Bazaar; {system} system, {m} stages, {cycles} elapsed cycles

entries.text: You founded the Star Bazaar in {system} and raised {n} of its {m} stages. Idris kept the plans weighted with a buyer's sample case. Workers ate beside those plans and traced where their counters would go.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, founded Bazaar; {system} system, {n} stages done, {m} total stages

entries.text: You founded the Star Bazaar in {system}, with {m} stages to build. No stage is built. Idris laid samples across the plans while builders took measurements. The crew had a site to point to, even without a hall to stand in.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, founded Bazaar with no completed stage; {system} system, {m} total stages

entries.text: The Star Bazaar stayed among Idris's sketches. He kept them with the price slips he took to lunch. Buyers who asked for a stall could point to a drawing, but could not stand there.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, Bazaar never founded; no specific placeholders

entries.text: At the Wing of Holds, wide racks were built for the Flagship's cargo. Its hold grew larger. Loaders could fit more of a buyer's order under the same hatch.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, Wing of Holds and larger Flagship hold; no specific placeholders

entries.text: You raised the Wing of Reach, with signal masts above its gallery. Hubs could reach farther. Clerks farther from a hub could put its deliveries on their boards.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, Wing of Reach and longer hub reach; no specific placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Tolls gave the clerks a hall for their counts. Worlds paid more tax to your company. Idris waited while each world clerk checked the sum again.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, Wing of Tolls and higher world tax; no specific placeholders

entries.text: You raised the Wing of Benches, a room of shared tools. New workshops cost less to build. Idris could leave more credits for the stock their crews would need.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, Wing of Benches and cheaper workshop construction; no specific placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Lamps put light over the Flagship's loading dock. Its hold grew larger. Crews could lay out more of Idris's parcels before deciding what would fit.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, Wing of Lamps and larger Flagship hold; no specific placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Couriers gave the worlds a stair for sending up their accounts. Your company took more tax from those worlds. A courier held the folded sheet flat while Idris checked what each name now owed.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, Wing of Couriers and higher world tax; no specific placeholders

entries.text: {names} is still an Outpost. A dock hand there keeps a jar for blooms beside the bunk. Buyers write the names of the people who will carry their parcels home. Idris keeps those names on the wrapping.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, world still at Outpost; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {n} worlds remain Outposts. At their posts, a buyer still knows who will carry each parcel home. Idris writes the names on the wrapping, even when the order only asks for blooms.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, worlds still at Outpost; {n} worlds, no names supplied

entries.text: {names} is a Village now, grown through your trade. Dock hands have homes beyond the shift rooms. A child waits at a kitchen table while a parent trims blooms for the market.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, world grown to Village; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are Villages now, {n} worlds grown through your trade. Dock hands have homes beyond the shift rooms. Children wait at kitchen tables while their parents trim blooms for market. The price board shares a wall with notices for lessons.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, worlds grown to Village; {names} is a plural ready list, {n} worlds

entries.text: {names} has become a Town through your trade. Cloth sellers live above their stalls, away from the loading shifts. A tailor's child gives directions by streets missing from Idris's early maps.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, world grown to Town; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are Towns now, {n} places your trade helped raise. Cloth sellers live above their stalls. Their children walk to lessons past street signs Idris no longer knows by heart.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, worlds grown to Town; {names} is a plural ready list, {n} worlds

entries.text: With your trade, {names} grew into a City. Dressmakers and dock crews live along streets that run beyond the port. A worker takes a parcel across town for a sister's wedding. Idris has to ask which way.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, world grown to City; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are Cities now, {n} worlds grown through your trade. Dressmakers share streets with dock crews and teachers. A wedding parcel can cross a whole district without passing the port. Idris asks for street names with his orders.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, worlds grown to City; {names} is a plural ready list, {n} worlds

entries.text: {names} became a Metropolis through your trade. Whole districts make and mend what once came through a dock counter. A silk worker rides home past streets where nobody knows the company name. There is a place set for them there.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, world grown to Metropolis; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are Metropolises now, {n} worlds your trade helped raise. Families live far beyond the old docks, among shops Idris has never visited. After a shift among silk rolls, a worker rides home through streets full of other lives.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, worlds grown to Metropolis; {names} is a plural ready list, {n} worlds

entries.text: No world grew through your trade. Idris kept looking from the price slips to the dock. At your posts, the same shift rooms held the same bunks. There was no new street beyond them.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, no world grew; no specific placeholders

entries.text: You brought life back to the dead world {names}. No more cargo would be mined there. A loader put a work coat on a hook at home. Idris sent blooms for the table.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, dead world reclaimed; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are living worlds again, {n} places with homes on the old mining ground. Crews hang their work coats beside kitchen shelves. Idris used to ask what could be taken out. The orders now carry blooms for people staying there.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, dead worlds reclaimed; {names} is a plural ready list, {n} worlds

entries.text: The Flagship built a place for trade or mining. A crew kept its cargo desk and put your company stamp beside it. Idris had a name to ask for when he called.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a trading post or mining platform built by the Flagship; no specific placeholders

entries.text: The Flagship built {n} trading posts and mining platforms. Crews kept the cargo desks and the stock lists there. Idris learned who to ask for before he asked the price.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, trading posts and mining platforms built by the Flagship; {n} combined total

entries.text: Your company reached {n} systems. Price slips crossed those gaps, each with a clerk's hand in the margin. Idris learned how long a reply could take when the buyer lived under another sun.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, company reach; {n} systems, at least two

entries.text: At its largest, your fleet was a lone {ship}. Idris could put a buyer's whole order against the space in that hold. The crew heard what he promised before they packed it.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, peak fleet of a single ship; {ship} is a singular ship type name

entries.text: At its largest, your fleet held {n} {ship} hulls. Idris could offer cargo space before a buyer finished asking. The crews waited by the pay desk while the ship upkeep sheet was read.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, peak fleet; {n} ships, {ship} is a singular ship type name

entries.text: You started a route. Idris could trace a cargo's planned journey beside its price. The crew checked that line before tying the parcels.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a route started; no specific placeholders

entries.text: You started {n} routes. On Idris's sheets, cargo had places to go as well as prices. Crews checked those lines before tying the parcels.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, routes started; {n} routes

entries.text: You removed a route from the plan. Idris crossed its arrival off his working sheet. A clerk had to be told that cargo would no longer come that way.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a route removed, after routes beat; no specific placeholders

entries.text: You removed {n} routes from the plan. Idris crossed their arrivals off his working sheets. Dock clerks had to be told which arrivals to rub off their boards. He left room for their replies.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, routes removed, after routes beat; {n} routes

entries.text: Your people learned a new skill. Idris tried the lesson on the back of a price slip. A crew hand checked it before he used it on an order.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a skill learned; no specific placeholders

entries.text: Your people learned {n} skills. Lessons shared space with Idris's price slips. When a lesson worked, a crew hand passed the marked page along.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, skills learned; {n} skills

entries.text: You built a place where goods could be made or passed on. Idris took a buyer's sample to the new work desk. The people there checked the stock before they heard his price.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a workshop, Fabric or hub built; no specific placeholders

entries.text: You built {n} places for making goods or passing them on. Idris carried samples between their desks. The people working there knew what was missing from an order before he could finish reading it.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, workshops, Fabric and hubs built; {n} combined total

entries.text: The Flagship reached a signal sent into the dark. Idris wrote the reply on the board before he filed the cargo slips. There was a voice behind that line, even if the call was old.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a signal answered by the Flagship; no specific placeholders

entries.text: {n} signals brought the Flagship off its usual work. Idris filed their replies beside his orders. On those pages, people had asked for more than a price.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, signals answered by the Flagship; {n} signals

entries.text: A signal went quiet without an answer from your Flagship. Idris kept its last mark on the board. He could say where the ship had been. He could not say who was still listening.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a signal went quiet unanswered; no specific placeholders

entries.text: The board lost {n} signals before your Flagship could answer. Idris kept their last known positions beside the orders he had filled. The pages did not say whether anyone still waited.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, signals went quiet unanswered; {n} signals

entries.text: A world ended a cycle short of what it needed. Idris read the need sheet beside the sales. At a dock counter, someone folded an order slip and put it back in a pocket.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a world-cycle with an unmet need; no specific placeholders

entries.text: {n} times, a world ended a cycle without all it needed. The same world could appear on that list again. Idris read it beside the sales, with a thumb holding each page flat. At the counters, people kept order slips for cargo that had not come.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, unmet needs; {n} occurrences counted per world per cycle, not elapsed cycles

entries.text: Relief credits kept the company going when it could not carry itself. Idris signed the receipt without his usual talk. The crew waited until it was stamped before they unpacked their work things.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, relief credits kept the company alive; no specific placeholders

entries.text: Relief credits kept the company going {n} times. Idris held his hand over the same line on each form. Each time, the crew waited for the stamp before setting out their work things.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, relief credits kept the company alive; {n} occasions

entries.text: The Bureau took a ship against the company's debt. Its clerk waited while the crew brought their things ashore. Idris stood beside the cargo ramp. There was no price left for him to discuss.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, a ship repossessed for debt; no specific placeholders

entries.text: The Bureau took {n} ships against the company's debt. The clerks read the forms slowly and let each crew collect its things. Idris learned to leave a space beside the ramp for the bags.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, ships repossessed for debt; {n} ships

entries.text: Idris stops turning pages when he reaches these entries in the company book.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, single sentence before the decisive-moments list; no specific placeholders

entries.text: Across your worlds, clerks say Idris's name before they ask for his order. A place is made at their tables while his ships are still coming in. He leaves the prices out of his reply.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, warm response from the worlds, before win closing; no specific placeholders

entries.text: Across your worlds, the smile still marks the company counters. Replies come addressed to {company}, with no word for Idris. He reads past the heading, then moves his thumb back to it.
entries.place: End screen, Idris, cold response from the worlds, before win closing; {company} company name

entries.text:
A garrison courier waits by the new hall's notice board. He has brought a letter for {company}. Sela Oru clears a patch of the long table for him.

The fleets you supply stood at the border without firing. The quarrel stopped when they arrived. Crews from the post check the terms with their fingers.

The Bureau clerk sets down the supplier record. She waits for Sela to finish reading the letter.
entries.place: End screen, The Quiet Fleets, scene opening; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name, {system} Bazaar system

entries.text:
The letter begins with thanks. Beneath it, the garrison has listed what it needs next.

Sela smooths the page where the courier's thumb held it. She puts the request beside the terms, where anyone can read. He pulls up a chair and helps her check it.
entries.place: End screen, The Quiet Fleets, scene close; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name

entries.text:
The racks of arms along the new hall are full. A depot clerk lays an order book before Sela Oru. His thumb holds her place while the Bureau clerk waits.

{company} is entered as supplier of record. Fleets wait for cargo, then follow the latest paid order. At a border post, the flags of either side share a purchase order.

The Bureau clerk asks for copies before the next dispatch. Sela reaches for the book. The depot clerk keeps his thumb on the page.
entries.place: End screen, The Full Racks, scene opening; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name, {system} Bazaar system

entries.text:
The depot clerk says the copies cannot be sent. The Bureau clerk thanks him and leaves her request to be filed.

A loader brings a crate for the border post. Sela looks for its flag on the order. The clerk puts his finger on the line that says who paid.
entries.place: End screen, The Full Racks, scene close; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name

entries.text:
Someone has left a lamp in the empty berth. Sela Oru walks past the new hall to reach it. She stops where a hull used to hide the far wall.

The Bureau took a ship against your debt. The clerk read the form slowly and waited for each name. Sela stood here while the crew carried their bags ashore.

The crews rebuilt from what the Bureau left. The Bazaar stands, with a hull still missing from her old plan. A dock hand waits with a fresh charge for the lamp.
entries.place: End screen, The Hull She Lost, repossession win, scene opening; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name, {system} Bazaar system

entries.text:
The dock hand bends to lift the lamp. Sela steps aside so he can change its charge.

He sets it back where the gangway used to rest. She checks that it is lit before she goes. She does not ask who keeps it there.
entries.place: End screen, The Hull She Lost, scene close; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name

entries.text:
The departure bell reaches Sela Oru through the hall's glass. She turns before the guests do. A loaded hull is moving clear of the dock.

The charter cargo is in. The Bazaar opened within its term. Out on the lanes, your crews kept going when signals came. Calls rarely faded without an answer.

A dock hand brings her a chair. She rests her palm on its back and watches the hull.
entries.place: End screen, No Hull Sat Still, many signals answered and few missed, scene opening; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name, {system} Bazaar system

entries.text:
The last departure clears the glass. The dock hand leaves the chair where she can see the lanes.

Sela checks the sky beyond the ship, then the space behind it. The bell falls still. She sits. Her palms lie flat on her knees.
entries.place: End screen, No Hull Sat Still, scene close; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name

entries.text:
The chart will not lie flat on the new table. Sela Oru holds its curled edge with her wrist. A worn pencil rests beside a ring round a distant world.

The Flagship found the way to places no clerk could name. Your crews built posts there and stayed. Their calls have come through to the Bazaar.

Someone asks Sela to mark the route for the next crew. She puts her pencil on the old ring.
entries.place: End screen, The Long Way Round, many worlds explored and established, scene opening; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name, {system} Bazaar system

entries.text:
Sela draws the route slowly enough for the waiting pilot to copy. She marks where the long cold stretch begins.

The pilot asks what it is like out there. She rests her finger on the ring. "There are people there now," she says.
entries.place: End screen, The Long Way Round, scene close; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name

entries.text:
The late watch has a chair turned toward the radio. Sela Oru takes it while the hall is still full. Someone sets a cup beside her.

Your fleet grew, and the worlds rarely had to wait for supplies. Sela kept a list for each watch. The crews have worked through those lists.

The lamps are on in the Bazaar. A dock hand asks whether she wants the radio turned down. She shakes her head.
entries.place: End screen, The Night Watch, large peak fleet and few unmet needs, scene opening; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name, {system} Bazaar system

entries.text:
The cup has gone cold. Sela wraps her hands round it without drinking.

No ship calls. She turns the chair a little nearer the radio. She leaves it on and loosens her grip on the cup.
entries.place: End screen, The Night Watch, scene close; {company} company, {ceo} full CEO name

entries.text: The Star Bazaar stands in {system}, all {m} stages raised in {cycles} cycles. Your crews signed off the Foundations, Halls, Towers and Great Hall. A builder sets her gloves beside a powder rack, clear of the loading shift.
entries.place: End screen beat, finished Bazaar, win only; {system} site system, {m} total stages, {cycles} cycles taken

entries.text: You founded the Star Bazaar in {system}. Your crews completed {n} of its {m} stages. Sela kept the unfinished loads on a separate sheet. A crew can point to each finished part and say who worked there.
entries.place: End screen beat, founded Bazaar with stages completed; {system} site system, {n} completed stages, {m} total stages

entries.text: You marked the Star Bazaar site in {system}. None of its {m} stages has been built. Sela put the first load on her sheet. The crew knew where to put cargo before there was a floor.
entries.place: End screen beat, founded Bazaar with no stage completed; {system} site system, {m} total stages

entries.text: No Star Bazaar site bears your company's name. Sela kept a clean sheet for its first cargo list. There is no shared hall where the far posts can meet.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bazaar never founded; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Holds gave the Flagship a bigger hold. Sela checked the space with a loader's tape. There was room for cargo that would once have waited ashore.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Holds chosen, larger Flagship hold; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Reach let your hubs serve farther worlds. Sela drew the wider reach on the supply charts. Dock crews beyond the old line could ask a hub for what they lacked.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Reach chosen, longer hub reach; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Tolls raised the tax your worlds paid. A clerk read the higher sum to a dock hand. He took the receipt back to the crew who had sent him.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Tolls chosen, higher world tax; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Benches made new workshops cost less to build. Sela kept the lower build bills with her spare plans. A crew needed fewer credits before it could set its tools down.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Benches chosen, lower workshop build cost; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Lamps added more room to the Flagship's hold. Loaders could fit a larger cargo beneath its straps. Sela checked where each crate would sit before she signed the loading sheet.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Lamps chosen, larger Flagship hold; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Couriers raised the tax your worlds paid. Bureau clerks carried the counts up its stair. A crew down below waited for its copy before going back to work.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Couriers chosen, higher world tax; no special placeholders

entries.text: {names} is still an Outpost. Its dock crew know whose bunk is empty on each watch. The lamp over the scales lights faces they all know.
entries.place: End screen beat, world still at Outpost; {names} single world name

entries.text: {n} worlds are still Outposts. The dock crews there still know every name on their shift. On Sela's supply sheets, each small post takes a line of its own.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds still at Outpost; {n} world count

entries.text: {names} grew into a Village as your loads reached it. Homes spread beyond the rooms kept for visiting crews. A loader can finish a shift and walk to a kitchen of her own.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to Village; {names} single world name

entries.text: {names} grew into {n} Villages as your loads reached them. Homes spread beyond the rooms kept for visiting crews. Loaders began ending their shifts at tables their families had set.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Village; {names} ready world list with plural verb, {n} world count

entries.text: {names} became a Town with the trade you brought. The depot is no longer the only place to find work. A fitter can send her child to school before taking a shift.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to Town; {names} single world name

entries.text: {names} became {n} Towns with the trade you brought. The depots are no longer the only places to find work. Fitters can send their children to school before taking a shift.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Town; {names} ready world list with plural verb, {n} world count

entries.text: {names} grew into a City on the goods your crews brought. A depot fitter rides home past streets that were blank on Sela's chart. At his stop, people are already waiting to ride to the next shift.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to City; {names} single world name

entries.text: {names} grew into {n} Cities on the goods your crews brought. Depot fitters ride home past streets that were blank on Sela's charts. At each stop, people are already waiting to ride to the next shift.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to City; {names} ready world list with plural verb, {n} world count

entries.text: {names} became a Metropolis through the trade you kept bringing. Whole districts have grown beyond sight of the docks. People rent homes there without ever asking which ship will take them away.
entries.place: End screen beat, world grown to Metropolis; {names} single world name

entries.text: {names} became {n} Metropolises through the trade you kept bringing. Whole districts have grown beyond sight of the docks. People rent homes there without ever asking which ship will take them away.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Metropolis; {names} ready world list with plural verb, {n} world count

entries.text: No world rose to a new tier through your trade. Sela's supply charts have no larger settlements to mark. The dock crews worked among the same bunks and loading racks they knew before.
entries.place: End screen beat, no world grew at all; no special placeholders

entries.text: {names} came back to life with the supplies you sent. The mining platform became a trading post. A cook wrote a meal list where the mining shifts had been.
entries.place: End screen beat, dead world brought back to life; {names} single reclaimed world name

entries.text: {names} are living worlds again. You brought {n} dead worlds back with supplies. Their mining platforms became trading posts, with cooks setting meal tables in the old tool rooms.
entries.place: End screen beat, dead worlds brought back to life; {names} ready world list with plural verb, {n} reclaimed world count

entries.text: Your Flagship built a place for a trading or mining crew. Sela checked its supply list before she checked the build stamp. People had to live beside the work once the ship flew on.
entries.place: End screen beat, Flagship built a trading post or mining platform; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Flagship built {n} trading posts and mining platforms. Sela checked their supply lists before she checked the build stamps. Each mark on the chart meant a crew who had stayed behind.
entries.place: End screen beat, trading posts and mining platforms built by Flagship; {n} combined count

entries.text: Your company reached {n} systems. Sela kept a supply chart for each stretch beyond the jump. The next crew out could ask someone what waited on the other side.
entries.place: End screen beat, systems reached, at least a pair; {n} system count

entries.text: The fleet never grew beyond a {ship} hull. Sela had to fit each route around what that ship could carry. When it came in, the dock crew knew whose boots would reach the gangway.
entries.place: End screen beat, largest fleet held a single ship; {ship} singular ship type name

entries.text: At its largest, your fleet held {n} {ship} hulls. Sela kept spare plans for a ship that failed to arrive. More crews had a berth to find when their watch was done.
entries.place: End screen beat, largest fleet, not final fleet; {n} peak ship count, {ship} singular ship type name

entries.text: You started a cargo route. Sela read its load sheet and kept a spare plan. At either end, someone could ask when the ship would come.
entries.place: End screen beat, route started; no special placeholders

entries.text: You started {n} cargo routes. Sela read their load sheets and kept spare plans. Behind each line on the chart were people waiting to load or unload.
entries.place: End screen beat, routes started; {n} route count

entries.text: You removed a route from the chart. Sela kept its old load sheet with a line through it. A loading crew no longer had that ship on its list.
entries.place: End screen beat, route removed, follows routes started; no special placeholders

entries.text: You removed {n} routes from the chart. Sela kept the old load sheets with lines through them. Crews had to check the new lists before they set cargo out.
entries.place: End screen beat, routes removed, follows routes started; {n} removed route count

entries.text: Your people learned a skill they had not brought aboard. Sela made room for it in the crew's notes. Someone else could follow the steps without waiting for the hand who knew them.
entries.place: End screen beat, skill learned; no special placeholders

entries.text: Your people learned {n} skills. The notes have grease marks where a tired hand held them. Sela had the pages copied for the next watch.
entries.place: End screen beat, skills learned; {n} learned skill count

entries.text: You built a place to make goods or send them onward. Sela put its work on the supply plan. People had somewhere to report for a shift.
entries.place: End screen beat, workshop, Fabric or hub built; no special placeholders

entries.text: You built {n} places to make goods or send them onward. Sela put their shifts beside the fleet's load lists. People had somewhere to report for work.
entries.place: End screen beat, workshops, Fabric and hubs built; {n} combined building count

entries.text: The Flagship went to a signal from beyond the trade lanes. Sela took its bearing before she read the next load sheet. Your crew saw what had kept the call going.
entries.place: End screen beat, signal answered by Flagship; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Flagship answered {n} signals off the trade lanes. Sela kept their bearings among her supply notes. Your crew saw places no standing order would have taken them.
entries.place: End screen beat, signals answered by Flagship; {n} answered signal count

entries.text: A signal went quiet without an answer from your Flagship. Sela kept its bearing after the mark had left the board. There was no reply she could put beside it.
entries.place: End screen beat, signal went quiet unanswered; no special placeholders

entries.text: {n} signals went quiet without an answer from your Flagship. Sela kept the bearings after their marks had left the board. None of those lines had a reply beside it.
entries.place: End screen beat, signals went quiet unanswered; {n} unanswered signal count

entries.text: A world ended a cycle short of what it needed. At a depot, someone read the delivery sheet again before handing it back. Sela kept that shortfall beside the loads that did get through.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world short of needs at cycle end, counted per world per cycle; no special placeholders

entries.text: {n} times, a world's needs were still short at cycle end. Depot clerks checked the cargo lists and sent the shortfalls back. Sela kept those pages beside the lists of what got through.
entries.place: End screen beat, needs short at cycle end, counted per world per cycle; {n} occurrences, not elapsed cycles

entries.text: You needed relief credits to keep the company going. Sela put the payment on the supply sheet. A crew could plan another shift before it had to pack.
entries.place: End screen beat, relief credits kept company alive; no special placeholders

entries.text: Relief credits kept the company going {n} times. Sela kept each payment on her supply sheets. Crews waited to learn whether they could set out their tools again.
entries.place: End screen beat, relief credits kept company alive; {n} relief payment count

entries.text: The Bureau repossessed a ship against your debt. Its clerk waited while the crew took their bags ashore. Sela checked the list of what they could carry off.
entries.place: End screen beat, ship repossessed for debt; no special placeholders

entries.text: The Bureau repossessed {n} ships against your debt. Its clerks read the forms slowly and waited for the crews. Sela checked each list of bags before a gangway was drawn back.
entries.place: End screen beat, ships repossessed for debt; {n} repossessed ship count

entries.text: These are the entries Sela kept at the front of her book.
entries.place: End screen beat, single sentence before decisive moment list; no special placeholders

entries.text: The border posts are quiet when Sela calls. A dock hand asks after her crew before asking for a load. She lowers her shoulders while she listens.
entries.place: End screen beat, warm Military worlds, win only, immediately before scene close; no special placeholders

entries.text: At the border posts, clerks ask for the order before a name. The racks are full, and voices stay low around them. Sela holds her coat shut while she listens.
entries.place: End screen beat, cold Military worlds, win only, immediately before scene close; no special placeholders

entries.text:
A child at the new ring of homes will not leave the lift.

Her mother stamps on the floor ahead. It gives back no thin ring of metal. Marek waits beside her with a bag of spare bolts. The next crew's shift is posted beside the lift. Behind the windows, the Star Bazaar is lit.

A Bureau clerk has come to count the homes. They stand on the ingot, alloy and plate your crews brought. He finds their form and smooths it on his knee.
entries.place: End screen, The Footing, scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
The child puts a foot out. Marek keeps his bag still while she presses her weight down.

Her mother takes off her work gloves. They walk past him toward their home. Marek listens until their steps fade. Nothing rattles beneath them.
entries.place: End screen, The Footing, scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
A worker sets her lamp on the Bazaar's new stone floor. White dust rings its base.

The Bureau clerk asks where she lives. She points to the name on her work coat. He turns the page toward her. The place is listed as uninhabited.

Marek stands beside her. Behind the clerk, ingot, alloy and plate are stacked for sale. Her crew's old cut has no seam left to follow. The next cut is already marked.
entries.place: End screen, The Strip, scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
The clerk asks her to sign beneath the entry. She wipes the dust from her fingers first. She reads it again before she signs.

He thanks her and puts the page away. Marek lifts the lamp for her. A pale ring stays on the floor.
entries.place: End screen, The Strip, scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
Marek pulls at a drawer in the Bazaar office. It sticks. The old shortage reports have bent against the wood.

A worker waits with the opening page. She sees her own hand on the top report. Back at her post, she wrote it while the shift ate what was left.

The hall outside is full of voices. Marek takes the report out and lays it beside the page. The worker pulls up a chair.
entries.place: End screen, The Long Shift, scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
He signs the opening page after the others. The worker waits while he holds the pen.

Marek smooths her old report and puts it back. This time the drawer shuts. He leaves the key in it.
entries.place: End screen, The Long Shift, scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
Someone has brought a stone from a mining platform to the Bazaar. It rests on a work coat by Marek's boots.

The crew took it from the cut he went down to see. He remembers lifting a handful there and setting it back. Dust still sits in the sleeves of the coat.

A Bureau clerk waits to list the gift. Marek crouches beside it. The crew have left the face with the tool marks showing.
entries.place: End screen, Down the Seams, scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
Marek sets the stone below the hall's beam. The clerk writes down its weight.

Marek asks him to leave room beneath it. The crew give their names for that line. Marek holds the page steady while they spell them.
entries.place: End screen, Down the Seams, scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
Marek cannot get the note to lie flat. An old yard man sent it wrapped round a spare bolt.

Around him, guests fill the Bazaar. Some know his voice from a call. Others have brought a pod tag or an old tool case. Nobody asks for a speech.

The note says, you picked up. Marek sets the bolt on its corner. Beside it lies the list of lanes he put to work when the calls came.
entries.place: End screen, The Man Who Picked Up, scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
The note goes beside the signal board. Marek presses its corners flat with his thumb.

Someone calls his name from the hall. He sets down the spare bolt and turns before they finish.
entries.place: End screen, The Man Who Picked Up, scene close; no placeholders

entries.text:
The Bureau clerk cannot find room for the fleet form. The bread is being passed across the crew's table.

Marek draws in his elbows to make space. Every pilot who brought your goods fits along the bench. The Bazaar fills the window behind them.

The clerk reads the list of ships. Marek says each name before the clerk reaches it. Then the clerk asks, politely, how many more are planned.
entries.place: End screen, The Thin Fleet, scene opening; no placeholders

entries.text:
Marek turns the form over. He writes nothing on the blank side.

The clerk waits. Marek shakes his head and passes the bread. At the far end, a pilot takes it without getting up.
entries.place: End screen, The Thin Fleet, scene close; no placeholders

entries.text: The Star Bazaar stands in {system}, with all {m} stages raised. Foundations, Halls, Towers and Great Hall took {cycles} cycles. Marek knows whose hands set the stone beneath the benches.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bazaar completed; {system} is its system, {m} stages, {cycles} elapsed cycles

entries.text: The Star Bazaar was founded in {system}. Your crews raised {n} of its {m} stages. Marek checked each finished joint before he signed the work sheet.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bazaar founded with stages done; {system} is its system, {n} completed stages of {m} total

entries.text: You founded the Star Bazaar in {system}. None of its {m} stages was raised. The crews had a site on their cargo sheets. They had no finished work there to put their names to.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bazaar founded with no stages done; {system} is its system, {m} total stages

entries.text: You never founded the Star Bazaar. Its name stayed on a loose sheet above Marek's bench. Crews read it while waiting for their next load.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bazaar never founded; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Holds gave the Flagship more room for cargo. Marek checked the hold against his load sheets. The crew could pack more than the old chalk line allowed.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Holds, larger Flagship hold; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Reach let hubs serve worlds farther away. Names beyond the old reach could go on a hub's list. Marek left space beside them for the goods their crews needed.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Reach, longer hub reach; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Tolls made your worlds pay more tax. The worlds' clerks had larger sums to send up. Marek kept their receipts with his parts orders.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Tolls, higher world tax; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Benches made new workshops cost less to build. Marek rubbed the old build price off his slate. He left the space for the crew's list of tools.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Benches, lower workshop build cost; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Lamps gave the Flagship a bigger hold. Under its loading lamps, the crew marked out the added room. Marek checked that the last crate could clear the straps.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Lamps, larger Flagship hold; no placeholders

entries.text: The Wing of Couriers raised the tax paid by your worlds. The couriers carried the higher counts up to the Bureau. Marek checked the sums against the worlds on his supply sheet.
entries.place: End screen beat, Wing of Couriers, higher world tax; no placeholders

entries.text: {names} remains an outpost. The crew still shares a bench with the tool rack. A worker has hung a child's coat beside a shift jacket.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world still at Outpost; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {n} worlds remain outposts. Their crews still clear tools from the bench before eating. Children learn to keep their elbows clear of the parts trays.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds still at Outpost; {n} worlds, at least two

entries.text: {names} grew into a village through your trade. A fitter can walk home after a shift now. Her child keeps a place for her at a kitchen table.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world grown to Village; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are villages now, {n} worlds built up through your trade. Fitters leave their boots beneath kitchen benches after work. Their children know which pair to tug at.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Village; {names} is a plural list, {n} is its count

entries.text: Your trade helped {names} grow into a town. The school has benches of its own now. The teacher hands back the stools borrowed from the loading yard.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world grown to Town; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are towns now, {n} worlds raised through your trade. Their schools have benches built for children. The loading crews have their stools back.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Town; {names} is a plural list, {n} is its count

entries.text: Your trade helped {names} grow into a city. Fitters rent rooms along streets beyond the old loading yard. A fitter can change jobs without packing up her home.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world grown to City; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are cities now, {n} worlds grown through your trade. Workers move between jobs without leaving the streets they know. Their children give directions by the old loading yards.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to City; {names} is a plural list, {n} is its count

entries.text: {names} has become a metropolis through your trade. Crews from far docks live above shops near the old post. A retired loader points it out when his grandchildren visit.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world grown to Metropolis; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are metropolises now, {n} worlds built up through your trade. The old loading yards sit among whole districts of homes. Retired crews show their grandchildren where they used to eat.
entries.place: End screen beat, worlds grown to Metropolis; {names} is a plural list, {n} is its count

entries.text: No world grew through your trade. Work coats still hang above the same bunks. A worker folds a sketch of a larger room. It goes back in the coat pocket.
entries.place: End screen beat, no world grew; no placeholders

entries.text: {names} was dead rock when your people came. You brought it back to life, and mining there stopped. A former cutter tends a patch of green beside the post.
entries.place: End screen beat, a dead world reclaimed; {names} is a single world name

entries.text: {names} are living worlds again, {n} places reclaimed through your work. Mining stopped there. Hands that packed rock samples now check new leaves for frost.
entries.place: End screen beat, dead worlds reclaimed; {names} is a plural list, {n} is its count

entries.text: The Flagship built a place for a crew to work. They chalked a shift list beside the hatch. Marek put the crew's spares on his next parts order.
entries.place: End screen beat, a trading post or mining platform built by the Flagship; no placeholders

entries.text: Your Flagship built {n} trading posts and mining platforms. Each needed hands to fit the frame and stay to run it. Marek's parts lists reached places his old yard never served.
entries.place: End screen beat, combined trading posts and mining platforms built by the Flagship; {n} total built

entries.text: {company} reached {n} systems. Yard hands who had never shared a shift began sending each other parts lists. Marek checked the bolt sizes before he checked the greetings.
entries.place: End screen beat, systems reached by the company; {company} is its name, {n} total systems

entries.text: At its largest, the fleet had a {ship}. Marek kept its parts list in his coat. The crew knew where to find him when a bolt would not fit.
entries.place: End screen beat, largest fleet was a ship; {ship} is the singular ship type

entries.text: At its largest, the fleet had {n} {ship} hulls. Marek checked their upkeep before he ordered spares. Each hull put another crew's shift in your hands.
entries.place: End screen beat, largest fleet; {n} hulls, {ship} is the singular ship type

entries.text: You started a route for your goods. Marek wrote its ends on a parts slip. At the far dock, someone cleared a place to set the load.
entries.place: End screen beat, a route started; no placeholders

entries.text: You started {n} routes. Marek wrote down what each would carry before he counted the credits. At the far docks, hands made room among the waiting crates.
entries.place: End screen beat, routes started; {n} routes

entries.text: You closed a route you had started. Marek struck it from the cargo sheet. He kept the old sheet so the crews could check what had changed.
entries.place: End screen beat, a route removed, after routes started; no placeholders

entries.text: You closed {n} routes you had started. Crews had to read the cargo sheets again. Marek kept the old copies so each change could be traced.
entries.place: End screen beat, routes removed, after routes started; {n} routes

entries.text: Your people learned a skill. Marek had them try it before he filed the lesson. The next shift pulled up stools to watch.
entries.place: End screen beat, a skill learned; no placeholders

entries.text: Your people learned {n} skills. The notes passed between shifts, with grease on the corners. Marek kept the pages whose errors had been crossed out.
entries.place: End screen beat, skills learned; {n} skills

entries.text: You built a place where goods could be made or sent on. Its crew set up a bench before they unpacked the tools. Marek checked what they needed, down to the spare bolts.
entries.place: End screen beat, a workshop, Fabric or hub built; no placeholders

entries.text: You built {n} places where goods could be made or sent on. Crews set up their benches beside the stock lists. Each crew kept mugs there, with names scratched underneath.
entries.place: End screen beat, combined workshops, Fabric and hubs built; {n} total built

entries.text: The Flagship answered a signal. The crew laid down their yard tools and went to look. Marek read their report before he returned to the parts list.
entries.place: End screen beat, a signal answered by the Flagship; no placeholders

entries.text: The Flagship answered {n} signals. Crews left their other work to go and look. Marek read each report before he let the next shift take the desk.
entries.place: End screen beat, signals answered by the Flagship; {n} signals

entries.text: A signal faded without a reply from your Flagship. The crew had no report to bring back. Marek left space for it between the finished jobs.
entries.place: End screen beat, a signal went quiet unanswered; no placeholders

entries.text: {n} signals went quiet without an answer from your Flagship. Marek had no reports to put beside their marks. He kept those spaces on the work sheet.
entries.place: End screen beat, signals went quiet unanswered; {n} signals

entries.text: A world had unmet needs at a cycle's end. Its crew stretched the stock or worked around what had not come. Marek read the report with their names beside it.
entries.place: End screen beat, a world ended a cycle with unmet needs; no placeholders

entries.text: {n} times a world had unmet needs at a cycle's end. People stretched the stock or worked around what had not come. Marek read their reports with the crew lists beside him.
entries.place: End screen beat, unmet needs counted per world per cycle; {n} such instances, not cycles or goods

entries.text: Relief credits kept {company} running when its own credits ran short. Marek signed the receipt with the crew waiting across the desk. They could go back to work.
entries.place: End screen beat, relief credits kept the company alive; {company} is its name

entries.text: Relief credits kept {company} alive {n} times. Marek kept the receipts where he could see them. The crews behind those payments got more time to find paying work.
entries.place: End screen beat, relief credits kept the company alive; {company} is its name, {n} payments

entries.text: The Bureau took a ship against your debt. The clerk asked for a signature, then waited while the crew packed. Marek put their tools on his own bench.
entries.place: End screen beat, a ship repossessed for debt; no placeholders

entries.text: The Bureau took {n} ships against your debt. The clerks read the forms slowly while crews carried their tools to the dock. Marek made room for those tools at his own bench.
entries.place: End screen beat, ships repossessed for debt; {n} ships

entries.text: Marek marked these entries for anyone who takes the desk next.
entries.place: End screen beat, a sentence before the decisive moments list; no placeholders

entries.text: When Marek asks about the work, the crews make room on their bench. The stone beneath their boots holds. He sits without reaching for the parts book.
entries.place: End screen beat, warm worlds, just before scene close on a win; no placeholders

entries.text: The halls are loud, and the cut seams lie bare. Crews give Marek the weights he asks for. Their hands stay on the work. Nobody asks him to sit.
entries.place: End screen beat, cold worlds, just before scene close on a win; no placeholders

entries.text: Sela kept the Bureau's penalty beside the depot records. Bram Hale stayed at his post, and the company ledger stayed clean.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale bribery charge, Bureau fine paid; no placeholders

entries.text: Sela dismissed Bram Hale and signed the new depot contracts herself. The route cost more for a while, but no fine was hidden in its loads.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale dismissed, route costs rose for a while; no placeholders

entries.text: Sela found the payment to Bram Hale's accuser between two clean depot reports. She closes the book, but the thin edge of the receipt still shows.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale's accuser paid to withdraw complaint; no placeholders

entries.text: Idris paid the Bureau's penalty where every clerk could see. He kept Bram Hale at the counter and gave the clean record no extra polish.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale bribery charge, Bureau fine paid; no placeholders

entries.text: Idris dismissed Bram Hale and welcomed the new worker himself. The new contracts cost more for a while, and he did not bargain them down with a secret.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale dismissed, route costs rose for a while; no placeholders

entries.text: Idris paid Bram Hale's accuser to leave the complaint outside. At the end, one corner of that receipt still shows beneath the company guest book.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale's accuser paid to withdraw complaint; no placeholders

entries.text: Marek paid the Bureau's penalty and kept the stamped receipt with the depot sheet. Bram Hale stayed on the shift, under a clean company record.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale bribery charge, Bureau fine paid; no placeholders

entries.text: Marek dismissed Bram Hale and put the new contracts on the work board. The route cost more for a while, but every hand could trace why.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale dismissed, route costs rose for a while; no placeholders

entries.text: The payment to Bram Hale's accuser is not on Marek's work sheet. He still knows which blank line it belongs on.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale's accuser paid to withdraw complaint; no placeholders

entries.text: Tamsin paid the Bureau's penalty and kept Bram Hale's name on the depot card. The company record stayed clean enough to send back without a covering note.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale bribery charge, Bureau fine paid; no placeholders

entries.text: Tamsin dismissed Bram Hale and wrote the new worker's name on a fresh card. The route cost more for a while; she kept Bram's old card behind it.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale dismissed, route costs rose for a while; no placeholders

entries.text: Tamsin paid Bram Hale's accuser, and the complaint came back blank. She reads the clean card twice, then keeps it with the notes no clerk will see.
entries.place: End screen beat, Bram Hale's accuser paid to withdraw complaint; no placeholders

entries.text: After Bram Hale was accused of taking a bribe, you paid the Bureau's penalty and kept him at work; the company record stayed clean.
entries.place: Chronicle beat, Bram Hale bribery charge, Bureau fine paid; no placeholders

entries.text: You dismissed Bram Hale without paying a fine, and the route cost more while a new worker signed its contracts again.
entries.place: Chronicle beat, Bram Hale dismissed, route costs rose for a while; no placeholders

entries.text: You paid Bram Hale's accuser to withdraw the complaint; no mark went on the record, but the payment remained.
entries.place: Chronicle beat, Bram Hale's accuser paid to withdraw complaint; no placeholders

entries.text: Mera's sealed hold

The Ninth Tally's beacon is still calling. Freight clerk Pell sends you its last crew list. Her sister Mera signed the final shift. Pell has rubbed a hole beside that name. Other ships have logged the signal and gone on. She asks you to look.

The Ninth Tally is split along its spine. Mera's coat lies tucked into an empty bunk. Cutting the hold free keeps the Flagship here a while. Pulling the flight log is quick and earns a small sum. Then you leave the cargo sealed inside.
Cut into the hold
Take the flight log
The depot accepts the sealed crates. Cutting them free kept the Flagship at the wreck a while. Iven rubs the depot stamp with his thumb. Mera's coat stayed in its bunk.
The lot is wrapped for a buyer who never came. Iven finds Mera's name sewn into the cloth. Cutting it free kept the Flagship there a while. The empty bunks stay behind.
Iven lifts the heavy crates free. Grey dust fills the seams of his gloves. The lot is yours. The Flagship has spent time at the wreck, and Mera's flight log stays unread.
