The sealed tubs are still warm. Iven keeps his hands round a lid until the lift takes it. The lot is yours. The Flagship has waited through the work. Mera's bunk stays empty.
A depot clerk pays a small sum for the log. Mera wrote the last order over a torn line. You send Pell a copy. The hold stays sealed when you leave.
A broker pays a small sum for the log of ports and buyers. Mera pressed hard enough to mark the next page. Pell gets a copy. The cargo stays behind its seal.
A claim office pays a small sum for the log of claims and loads. Mera's pencil stops at an empty weight box. You send Pell the page. The hold stays sealed.
A clinic pays a small sum for the log of cold stops. Mera underlined the stop where cooling failed. You send Pell a copy. The cargo stays sealed inside.
The Bureau thanks Pell for her letter. The Ninth Tally remains overdue. She folds the reply along the crew list's crease.
Orven's relay lamp

Orven's lamp still marks the way through the debris. The Bureau lists his relay as closed. His pay stopped with that line. His voice comes through after the signal. He asks which dock still takes passengers. You hear him set the radio down before he coughs.

Orven grips the lamp switch with a cloth round his hand. Take him home for a small dock fee, and he gives you his stores. The lamp goes dark. Keep his shift and earn a small sum. The Flagship waits while he sleeps. He will still be the keeper.
Bring him to dock
Take his lamp shift
Orven gives you the relay's depot crates. You pay a small dock fee for him. He keeps the switch cloth in his fist through the flight. Behind you, the lamp goes dark. Ships must go round the debris.
Orven gives you the parcels traders left him. The gift tags are still tied on. You pay his small dock fee. He stands by the hatch until it opens. Behind you, the unlit passage must wait.
Orven gives you the relay's marked sacks. He checks each weight with a finger. You pay a small dock fee to bring him home. The lamp is out. Ships must take the way round.
Orven gives you his sealed jars. A ring on the shelf shows where each stood. You pay a small dock fee for him. He steps ashore. The lamp stays dark behind you.
The Flagship waits through Orven's shift. Haulers leave a small sum in the lamp box. Their depot marks fill his log. He wakes with the switch cloth pressed to his cheek. You give him back the watch.
The Flagship waits while Orven sleeps. Traders leave a small sum in the lamp box. Their buyers' names fill his log. He wakes and smooths his coat before taking the switch from you.
You keep the lamp while Orven sleeps. Haulers leave a small sum and log their loads. The Flagship waits through the shift. He wakes and checks the pencil weights before he sits down at the switch.
The Flagship waits through the watch. Haulers leave a small sum and log their cold cargo. Orven sleeps with his hand curled round nothing. When he wakes, you place the switch cloth back in it.
The Bureau's closed-relay form has no space for Orven's name. Passing crews still use it when they call.
Lio's missing pod

An automatic Bureau signal comes from a missing courier pod. Courier Lio's last message says a rescue ship took her crew after debris broke the pod's drive. She left an unused production charter sealed inside. Her coat is tied around its case so the finder will see it.

The empty pod holds Lio's flight record and sealed charter. Register the charter for a world you choose. It makes that world produce and store more for a while, but the Flagship waits a long time. Send the record for a small sum and leave sooner. The charter stays here.
Register the charter
Send the flight record
After a long wait, the charter is yours. You can use it at a world you choose. A red depot mark is stamped on its metal case. Iven unties Lio's coat and carries the case to the Flagship.
After a long wait, the charter is yours. You can use it at a world you choose. Bright cloth cushions the case. Iven folds Lio's coat and carries both to the Flagship.
After a long wait, the charter is yours. You can use it at a world you choose. Grey rock dust fills the case hinge. Iven frees it with a brush, then unties Lio's coat.
After a long wait, the charter is yours. You can use it at a world you choose. A dried green leaf lies beneath the case strap. Iven places it inside Lio's folded coat.
After the shorter wait, the Bureau pays a small sum for the flight record. Its last image shows Lio checking the cargo clamps before she leaves. You close the pod. The charter stays sealed inside.
After the shorter wait, the Bureau pays a small sum for the flight record. Its last image shows Lio tying bright cloth around a case. You close the pod. The charter stays sealed inside.
After the shorter wait, the Bureau pays a small sum for the flight record. Its last image shows Lio wiping grey dust from the controls. You close the pod. The charter stays sealed inside.
After the shorter wait, the Bureau pays a small sum for the flight record. Its last image shows Lio checking the heat in sealed trays. You close the pod. The charter stays sealed inside.
The Bureau adds your report to Lio's rescue file. The pod's signal stops. Her coat goes back to her.
Sella's closing meal

A station sends a closure call. Sella says she is its last caretaker. The workers left when the route moved, but their companies never collected the stock. The Bureau has ordered her to clear the rooms and leave. She asks one passing crew to witness the closing.

Sella meets you at the hatch. Behind her are company stock and a table set for the station's final meal. Load a lot into your company's storage and pay a small berth fee. Or sign the closure record and eat with her for a small sum. The Flagship waits a short while.
Load the company stock
Witness the closing
You load the sealed depot cases and pay the small berth fee. Red inspection marks cover their lids. Sella crosses the cases off her closing list. Iven carries the last one past the table.
You load the wrapped parcels and pay the small berth fee. Bright cloth shows through one torn corner. Sella crosses the lot off her closing list. The table stays ready for her final meal.
You load the heavy sacks and pay the small berth fee. Grey dust marks the empty floor. Sella crosses the lot off her closing list. Iven closes the bare store room.
You load the sealed trays and pay the small berth fee. Each lid is still warm. Sella crosses the lot off her closing list. Iven checks the cold room before she locks it.
The Flagship waits while you eat with Sella. Old depot stamps cover the metal plates. You sign the closure record, and she pays a small sum from the station fund. She clears the table.
The Flagship waits while you eat with Sella. She brings out the last clean tablecloth. You sign the closure record, and she pays a small sum from the station fund. She folds the cloth.
The Flagship waits while you eat with Sella. Grey dust lies in the workers' names cut into the table. You sign the closure record, and she pays a small sum from the station fund.
The Flagship waits while you eat with Sella. One green cutting stands in a cup by her plate. You sign the closure record, and she pays a small sum from the station fund.
The Bureau records the station as closed. Sella sends one last message: the table is clear, and she has booked passage out.
Dena's last test

The range tone stops before its check is done. Shift chief Dena signed the last test book. The Bureau can send a copy when your request reaches the desk. Iven listens to the tone again. He knows the pause where a crew should answer.

Dena's glove hangs from a tool rack. Beyond it, targets wait for the last test. Strip the rack for a lot, and the Flagship waits a while. Follow her book for a small sum, and it waits longer. The rack stays here. Iven rests his hand on the gate.
Take the tools
Trace the last test
The Flagship waits while Iven frees the lot from the rack. Dena scratched crew names into the clamps. He turns each name inward before stacking it. The last test stays unread.
You take the heavy cutters and drill. The Flagship waits through the work. Iven leaves Dena's glove on its hook. The crane still holds its crate. No hand comes to lower it.
The Flagship waits while you follow Dena's last test bearing. A depot clerk pays a small sum for the page. Iven holds a finger beneath the final blank line. The tools stay on their rack.
The Flagship waits while you follow Dena's notes into the rock field. A claim office pays a small sum for the copied depths. Her pencil snapped at the last mark. The crane keeps its crate.
The Bureau confirms that the range is closed. Dena's last test still has a space for the crew to sign.
Vela's garden hatch

A garden glows behind a glass hull. No visit is owed to it under the Plan. A chime brings a voice to the radio. Vela asks whether you have come for flowers or seed. Iven wipes the screen where her hand leaves a print. The print is on her side.

Vela opens the fogged hatch with a sleeve over her hand. Cut blooms for a small sum, and the Flagship waits through the work. Or pay a small toll for a bag of seed. The beds stay green. Vela keeps the shears on the table between you.
Cut the blooms
Take the seed
The Flagship waits while you cut. A dock buyer pays a small sum for the blooms. Their scent stays in Iven's sleeve. Vela takes the shears back. The bare beds show where he stood.
The Flagship waits through the cutting. A clinic pays a small sum for the blooms. Iven scrubs a stain from his glove. Vela lays the shears down beside the beds you left bare.
You pay Vela's small toll and take the bags of seed. She ties each bag with thread from her sleeve. The beds stay green. She puts the unused shears back in their drawer.
You pay Vela's small toll for the seed lot. She folds damp paper round each bag. Iven cups his hands beneath them. The beds stay green behind the hatch. The shears have not moved.
The garden is listed as tended. Vela asks you to add her name. There is room below the stamp.
Renn's waiting drive

Renn still runs the yard's test drive. The Bureau closed the yard after the drive proved faster than the approved hulls. He sends you the fit sheet with a thumbprint in oil. The drive would fit your Flagship. A buyer has asked him to stop the test.

Renn has kept the drive on its cradle. An oil ring marks where his cup stood. Fit it and the Flagship flies as fast as a Dart for good. The work takes a long wait. Sell it for a small sum and wait less. Renn holds out the buyer's note.
Fit the drive
Sell it to the buyer

Renn's crew fits the drive through a long wait. The Flagship now flies as fast as a Dart, for good. Iven sets his cup on the deck. For the first time, it stays where he puts it. The spare plates stay in the yard.
After a brief wait, a depot clerk pays a small sum for the drive. Renn wipes the cradle where it stood. The Flagship leaves at its old speed. Iven lifts his cup before the deck starts to shake.
The Bureau's yard file stays closed. Renn sends the crew a copy of the fit sheet, with the oil mark still on it.
The charter at the door

The last hall has a roof. The charter cargo waits for the Flagship at the dock. Every hand that built the Star Bazaar has signed its crate. Iven points to his name under a patch of dried glue. The hall lamps are dark. The crew waits for you to bring it in.

The Flagship docks with the signed charter cargo. The crew stands along the hall they built. Iven wipes his hands before taking the crate. Beyond him, the Star Bazaar's lamps are dark. You reach for the other handle. The crew makes room.
Carry the crate in
You carry the crate with Iven. He waits for the crew to gather before he breaks the seal. The hall lamps come on. He puts the lid down where every name can still be read. No order follows.
Iven spreads a cloth beneath the crate. You break the seal. A warm scent reaches the crew at the door. The lamps come on. He smooths the cloth where a builder has rested a hand.
You push the loaded cart beside Iven. He braces a foot against the wheel while you break the seal. The lamps come on. He holds the cart a moment longer, then lifts his foot.
The crate leaves a damp square on Iven's coat. You break the seal together. Warm air reaches the crew at the door. The lamps come on. He leaves his coat over the cart and goes to meet them.
Voltara's reactors run wild

Energy at Voltara costs less and pays less. Pavo Quill kept the reactors running past shift change. His meal sits untouched beside the controls. Cheap power leaves room in your budget. His crew must sell more to earn the same.
Grey blight on Tillam's terraces

Food at Tillam costs more and pays more. Grower Sella wipes grey dust from a dead leaf onto her sleeve. Her harvest crate is empty. A Seed Bank lets planet storage hold clearly more. Until then, each load costs more to bring home.
Ashgate's harvest comes in heavy

Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less. Clerk Nera's book lists half the harvest. Her son wheels the rest to the dock in a handcart. Buying costs less today. Nera needs the sacks sold before damp reaches the grain.
Voltara's crews go hungry

Food at Voltara costs more and pays more. Loader Venn folds his ration slip around a heel of bread. The Bureau thanks the crews for waiting. Your next load can pay more here. Venn keeps the slip for tomorrow.
Frost on Tillam

Energy at Tillam costs more and pays more. The heaters run without rest. Brindle scrapes frost from the inside of a duct with his cup. He asks when the next load comes. You check what it will cost to send it.
Ashgate lights every furnace

Energy at Ashgate costs more and pays more. Every foundry has relit for the new Plan. Brakeman Olan holds his coat against the furnace glare. He was meant to be home by now. The next load will cost more before it pays more.
Tillam's docks go on strike

Tillam's port is closed for a while. Routes touching Tillam are blocked. Dockhand Sella hangs her unpaid shift slips on the gate. The Bureau asks for time to review them. Hardy Strains reopens a closed planet a cycle sooner.
Ashgate seals its port

Ashgate's port is closed for a while. Routes touching Ashgate are blocked. Doctor Eda presses a notice to the glass with her bare palm. Her coat is still inside the sealed dock. Your crews wait outside with their cargo.
Voltara goes dark

Voltara's port is closed for a while. Routes touching Voltara are blocked after a grid fault. Clerk Neris holds a candle over the arrival book. She keeps a thumb on your ship's name. There is no berth she can give it.
A lender walks Tillam's market

Energy at Tillam costs less and pays less for now. Shylo Vane has bought the sellers' debts. Trader Senn empties his stock to settle his share. He rubs the old price from his board. You can buy cheaply from him today.
Ashgate's foreman says enough

Energy at Ashgate costs less and pays less. Foreman Dov Rennick sent his crew home after the shift met its target. He hangs the furnace key beside his child's coat. Your stock will pay less here. His hands have stopped shaking.
Voltara buys before the news

Energy at Voltara costs more and pays more. Wex said the far beacons had failed. They still shine above a dock stripped of stock. Buyer Eren holds an empty fuel can. Price Whisper shows next cycle's prices before you commit another load.
A family buys Ashgate's food

Food at Ashgate costs more and pays more. Corvale's family bought every food contract. He flattens a receipt beneath the canteen's empty bread tray. Your cargo can earn more here. The cook asks which name she should put on her order.
The inspector's count

Food at Voltara costs less and pays less. Inspector Pell marked the stores full on his form. Cook Venn turns an empty bin toward him. Pell asks for the bin's entry in the book. Your next sale pays less while they check.
Tillam's festival of founders

Food at Tillam costs more and pays more. The founders' festival has filled the halls. Cook Sella removes her mask to count the bread left. Your cargo can earn more here. She sets aside a crust before opening the kitchen door.
A ship leaves Tillam half empty

Food at Tillam costs less and pays less. A ship left for uncharted rock with room still in its hold. Cook Eren sells the food he saved for a friend aboard. He leaves her cup beside the till. The sale must pay for his own stay.
